value.zh: 孝惠皇帝諱衷，字正度，武帝第二子也。
value.en: Emperor Hui, whose personal name was Sima Zhong and courtesy name Zhengdu, was Emperor Wu’s second son.
value.literal: The Filial and Kind Emperor, taboo name Zhong, courtesy name Zhengdu, was the second son of Emperor Wu.

value.zh: 泰始三年，立爲皇太子，時年九歲。
value.en: In 267, when he was nine years old, he was named heir apparent.
value.literal: In the third year of Taishi, he was established as crown prince; at the time he was nine sui.

value.zh: 太熙元年四月己酉，武帝崩。
value.en: In the fourth month of the first year of Taixi, on the day jiyou, Emperor Wu died.
value.literal: In the first year of Taixi, on the jiyou day of the fourth month, Emperor Wu died.

value.zh: 是日，皇太子即皇帝位，大赦，改元爲永熙。
value.en: That same day the heir apparent ascended the throne, ordered a general amnesty, and adopted the reign title Yongxi.
value.literal: That same day the crown prince assumed the imperial throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Yongxi.

value.zh: 尊皇后楊氏曰皇太后，立妃賈氏爲皇后。
value.en: Empress Yang was elevated to empress dowager, and his consort Lady Jia was installed as empress.
value.literal: The empress, Lady Yang, was honored as empress dowager; Consort Jia was established as empress.

value.zh: 十二月丁亥，詔曰：「天禍晉邦，冢嗣莫繼。
value.en: On the dinghai day in the twelfth month an edict began: “Heaven scourges Jin, and no son of mine survives to succeed.
value.literal: On the dinghai day of the twelfth month an edict stated: “Heaven has punished the Jin state; no heir succeeds.

value.zh: 成都王穎自在儲貳，政績虧損，四海失望，不可承重，其以王還第。
value.en: Prince Ying proved unfit while heir apparent and has forfeited the trust of the realm, so he must be stripped of the succession and sent home to his fief.
value.literal: Prince Ying of Chengdu, while heir, failed in government; within the four seas hope was disappointed; he cannot bear the heavy charge; let him return to his residence as a prince.

value.zh: 豫章王熾先帝愛子，令問日新，四海注意，今以爲皇太弟，以隆我晉邦。
value.en: Prince Chi of Yuzhang, the late emperor’s favorite, grows in reputation every day, and he shall be named imperial younger brother and heir to steady the house of Jin.
value.literal: Prince Chi of Yuzhang was the late emperor’s beloved son; his fair fame grows daily; within the four seas all eyes turn to him; now let him be made imperial younger brother and heir to uplift our Jin state.

value.zh: 以司空越爲太傅，與太宰顒夾輔朕躬。
value.en: Minister of Works Prince Yue is appointed grand tutor to work beside Grand Steward Yong in guiding the throne.
value.literal: Let Minister of Works Yue be made grand tutor, together with Grand Steward Yong to flank and assist my person.

value.zh: 司徒王戎參錄朝政，光祿大夫王衍爲尚書左僕射。
value.en: Wang Rong shall join in supervising policy, and Wang Yan shall take the left vice directorship of the secretariat.
value.literal: Let Minister of Education Wang Rong participate in recording court governance; Household Grandee Wang Yan is made left vice director of the secretariat.

value.zh: 安南將軍虓、安北將軍浚、平北將軍騰各守本鎮。
value.en: Generals Xiao, Jun, and Teng are ordered to hold their existing commands.
value.literal: General Who Pacifies the South Xiao, General Who Pacifies the North Jun, and General Who Pacifies the North Teng each guard their original garrisons.

value.zh: 高密王簡爲鎮南將軍，領司隸校尉，權鎮洛陽；
value.en: Prince Jian of Gaomi becomes general who guards the south and acting metropolitan superintendent at Luoyang.
value.literal: Prince Jian of Gaomi is made general who guards the south, concurrently metropolitan superintendent, acting in authority at Luoyang;

value.zh: 東中郎將模爲寧北將軍、都督冀州，鎮于鄴；
value.en: Sima Mo moves to general who guards the north with Ji Province command, based at Ye.
value.literal: General of the Household Gentlemen of the East Mo is made general who guards the north and area commander for Ji Province, stationed at Ye;

value.zh: 鎮南大將軍劉弘領荊州，以鎮南土。
value.en: Liu Hong, general-in-chief who guards the south, keeps order in Jing Province.
value.literal: General-in-chief Who Guards the South Liu Hong holds Jing Province to secure the south.

value.zh: 周馥、繆胤各還本部，百官皆復職。
value.en: Zhou Fu and Miao Yin go back to their posts, and every minister returns to duty.
value.literal: Zhou Fu and Miao Yin each return to their original commands; the hundred officials all resume their posts.

value.zh: 齊王冏前應還第，長沙王乂輕陷重刑，封其子紹爲樂平縣王，以奉其嗣。
value.en: Prince Jiong ought long ago to have been sent to his domain, and Prince Yi suffered a cruel death, so enfeoff his son Shao as prince of Leping to preserve his line.
value.literal: Prince Jiong of Qi should earlier have returned to his residence; Prince Yi of Changsha was lightly subjected to heavy punishment; enfeoff his son Shao as prince of Leping county to continue his line.

value.zh: 自頃戎車屢征，勞費人力，供御之物皆減三分之二，戶調田租三分減一。
value.en: Because armies have marched again and again, palace supplies are cut by two-thirds, and the poll tax and land rent are each reduced by a third.
value.literal: Recently war-chariots have repeatedly marched, exhausting men and resources; articles for the imperial household are all reduced by two-thirds; household levies and field rent are each reduced by one-third.

value.zh: 蠲除苛政，愛人務本。
value.en: Harsh statutes are swept away so the people may return to their fields.
value.literal: Harsh government is remitted; the people are cherished and the root is sought.

value.zh: 清通之後，當還東京。」
value.en: Once peace is restored, the court will return to Luoyang.”
value.literal: After the realm is cleared and at peace, we shall return to the eastern capital.”

value.zh: 大赦，改元。
value.en: The edict ended with a general amnesty and a new reign title.
value.literal: A general amnesty; the era name was changed.

value.zh: 以河間王顒都督中外諸軍事。
value.en: Prince Yong of Hejian received overall command of every army.
value.literal: Prince Yong of Hejian was made area commander for all military affairs within and without.

value.zh: 夫乾坤定位，男女流形，伉儷之義同歸，貴賤之名異等。
value.en: Heaven and earth fixed their stations; men and women took their bodily shapes. Husband and wife share one moral purpose, even though rank divides high from low.
value.literal: As for Qian and Kun taking their positions, male and female receive their forms; the principle of husband and wife aims at the same end, yet the names of noble and base stand in different ranks.

value.zh: 若乃作配皇極，齊體紫宸，象玉床之連後星，喻金波之合羲璧。
value.en: Those who match the sovereign on high and share the body politic of the inner palace are figured as the jade couch tied to the queen’s asterism, as moonlight married to the solar disk.
value.literal: When one is paired with the supreme apex and shares the substance of the Purple Palace, it is likened to the jade couch linking to the rear stars, and compared to golden waves joining the Xi disk.

value.zh: 爰自敻古，是謂元妃；
value.en: In deepest antiquity she was known as the principal wife;
value.literal: From remote antiquity onward, she was called the chief consort;

value.zh: 降及中年，乃稱王后。
value.en: Later ages styled her queen.
value.literal: Descending to middle antiquity, she was then titled queen.

value.zh: 四人並列，光于帝嚳之宮；
value.en: Four consorts stood side by side and brought glory to Emperor Ku’s inner court;
value.literal: Four women stood ranked together, shining in the palace of Emperor Ku;

value.zh: 二妃同降，著彼有虞之典。
value.en: Two royal brides arrived together and entered the canonical record of Shun’s reign.
value.literal: Two consorts descended together, written into the canons of Yu’s age.

value.zh: 夏商以上，六宮之制，其詳靡得而聞焉。
value.en: For ages before Xia and Shang, no reliable detail survives about how the six wings of the harem were ordered.
value.literal: Above Xia and Shang, the regulations of the Six Palaces cannot be heard of in detail.

value.zh: 姬劉以降，五翟之規，其事可略而言矣。
value.en: From the Zhou and Han dynasties on, the graded “five pheasant” ritual for consorts can at least be sketched.
value.literal: From Ji and Liu onward, the rules of the five pheasant insignia may be spoken of in outline.

value.zh: 周禮，天子立一后、三夫人、九嬪、二十七世婦、八十一御妻，以聽王者內政。
value.en: The Rites of Zhou prescribe one empress, three chief consorts, nine ranked ladies, twenty-seven secondary wives, and eighty-one attendants to manage the sovereign’s domestic government.
value.literal: In the Rites of Zhou, the Son of Heaven establishes one queen, three ladies, nine bin, twenty-seven wives of rank, and eighty-one minor wives, to administer the king’s inner administration.

value.zh: 故婚義曰：「天子之與后，如日之與月，陰之與陽。」
value.en: The Meaning of Marriage therefore declares: “The emperor and his empress mirror sun and moon, yin and yang.”
value.literal: Therefore the Meaning of Marriage says: “The Son of Heaven and the queen are like sun and moon, yin and yang.”

value.zh: 由斯而談，其所從來遠矣。
value.en: Judged by such language, their institution reaches far back into antiquity.
value.literal: From this perspective, what they derive from is distant indeed.

value.zh: 故能母儀天宇，助宣王化，德均載物，比大坤維，宗廟歆其薦羞，穹壤俟其交泰。
value.en: Hence she sets the maternal standard for the realm, advances the king’s civilizing work, and bears creation as steadfastly as earth itself; the temple accepts her sacrifices gladly, and heaven and earth look to her union with the throne for peace.
value.literal: Thus she can be the motherly model for all under heaven, aid in spreading royal transformation, her virtue evenly bearing all things, comparable to the great sustaining power of Kun; the ancestral temple delights in her offerings, heaven and earth await her harmonizing union.

value.zh: 是以哲王垂憲，尤重造舟之禮；
value.en: That is why enlightened monarchs codify law and prize above all the royal wedding rite of “meeting across the boat.”
value.literal: Therefore wise kings hang forth statutes and especially esteem the rite of the built bridge;

value.zh: 詩人立言，先獎葛覃之訓。
value.en: The Classic of Poetry opens by honoring the lessons of “Ge Tan,” the ode on diligent royal ladies.
value.literal: The poets set forth words and first praise the instruction of “Ge Tan.”

value.zh: 後燭流景，所以裁其宴私；
value.en: Dimming the late-night lamp curbs excess in the privy chamber;
value.literal: The rear candle’s flowing light is the means to regulate their private banquets;

value.zh: 房樂希聲，是用節其容止。
value.en: Sparse music in the inner rooms reins in conduct at court and couch alike.
value.literal: Chamber music with sparse sound is the means to moderate their bearing.

value.zh: 履端正本，抑斯之謂歟！
value.en: Walking straight to set the root right—surely this is what those measures intend!
value.literal: Walking upright to rectify the root—is this not what is meant!

value.zh: 若乃娉納有方，防閑有禮，肅尊儀而修四德，體柔範而弘六義，陰教洽于宮闈，淑譽騰於區域。
value.en: When matches are arranged by rule, propriety fences passion, majesty guards ritual while the four womanly virtues are cultivated, gentle models enlarge the six canonical lessons, inner-chamber teaching fills the harem, and fair fame spreads beyond the capital.
value.literal: If betrothal and intake have proper method, fences and restraint have ritual, reverently honoring ceremony while cultivating the four virtues, embodying gentle norms while extending the six meanings, then women’s instruction permeates the palace, and good reputation rises through the regions.

value.zh: 則玄雲入戶，上帝錫母萌之符；
value.en: Then auspicious clouds cross the threshold and Heaven grants the token of fruitful motherhood;
value.literal: Then dark clouds enter the door, and the Supreme Lord grants the sign of motherhood’s sprouting;

value.zh: 黃神降徵，坤靈贊壽丘之道，終能鼎祚惟永，胤嗣克昌。
value.en: The divine Yellow Emperor sends portents; earth’s spirit blesses the birth-hill of sage-kings; the dynasty’s mandate endures and heirs thrive.
value.literal: The Yellow Spirit sends down omens; the spirit of Kun assists the way of Shouqiu; ultimately the tripod fortune can be everlasting and heirs flourish.

value.zh: 至若儷極虧閑，憑天作孽，倒裳衣于衽席，感朓側於弦望。
value.en: But women who reach the throne yet abandon modesty, who invoke Heaven while plotting harm, who turn proper dress upside down on the bed, and whose passions shift with every phase of the moon—
value.literal: As for those paired to the apex yet deficient in restraint, who rely on heaven to work calamity, who overturn upper and lower garments upon the mat, and feel lust askew at first quarter and full moon.

value.zh: 則龍漦結釁，宗周鞠為黍苗；
value.en: —dragon spit seals a fatal feud, and the Zhou heartland turns to weed-grown ruin;
value.literal: Then dragon-spittle knots disaster, and royal Zhou becomes nothing but millet shoots;

value.zh: 燕尾挻災，隆漢墜其枌社矣。
value.en: swallow-tail charms invite catastrophe, and even mighty Han loses its soil-and-millet shrines.
value.literal: Swallow tails draw calamity, and flourishing Han drops its mulberry altars.

value.zh: 自曹劉內主，位以色登，甄衛之家，榮非德舉。
value.en: Under the Cao and Liu courts, palace ladies rose by looks alone; clans such as the Zhens and Weis won favor without moral merit.
value.literal: Since the inner mistresses of Cao and Liu, position climbed by beauty; in the households of Zhen and Wei, glory was not raised by virtue.

value.zh: 淫荒挺性，蔑西郊之禮容；
value.en: Wanton temperaments mocked the solemn suburban liturgy reserved for the empress;
value.literal: Dissolute and wasteful by nature, they slighted the ritual bearing of the western suburb;

value.zh: 婉孌含辭，作南國之奇態。
value.en: Soft voices and studied phrases invented the freakish grace of southern entertainers.
value.literal: Soft loveliness holding coy phrases, they fashioned exotic manners of the southern states.

value.zh: 詖謁由斯外人，穢德於是內宣。
value.en: Sycophancy leaked beyond the palace gates while depravity was preached inside.
value.literal: Slanderous flattery thereby passed outward, and foul conduct was proclaimed within.

value.zh: 椒掖播晨牝之風，蘭殿絕河雎之響。
value.en: The harem aired the omen of women ruling like crowing hens; orchid halls no longer echoed the chaste songs of “Guan ju.”
value.literal: The pepper chambers spread the wind of the hen crowing at dawn; the orchid halls cut off the echo of “Guan ju” by the River.

value.zh: 永言彤史，大練之範逾微；
value.en: Forever the palace diarists wrote, yet the ideal of homespun austerity faded;
value.literal: Speaking long of the vermilion scribe, the model of coarse white silk grows ever fainter;

value.zh: 緬視青蒲，脫珥之猷替矣。
value.en: Looking back to mat audiences where consorts remonstrated, the counsel of tearing off earrings to warn the throne had vanished.
value.literal: Gazing afar at the green rushes, the strategy of casting off ear-jewels is replaced.

value.zh: 晉承其末，與世污隆，宣皇創基，功弘而道屈；
value.en: The Jin took up this fallen era and rose or fell with the times. Emperor Xuan laid the foundations: his deeds were grand, yet the moral course stayed cramped;
value.literal: Jin inherited the late age; with the world it sank and rose. Emperor Xuan founded the base—achievement broad yet the Way bent;

value.zh: 穆后一善，勣侔於十亂。
value.en: a single virtue in Empress Mu rivaled the merit of the “ten turbulent” worthies who saved a dynasty.
value.literal: one goodness of Empress Mu—merit equal to the Ten Disorderly Ones.

value.zh: 洎乎世祖，[1]始親選良家，既而帝掩紈扇，躬行請託。
value.en: Under Emperor Wu [1] the court at first picked brides from respectable houses; soon the sovereign waved his silk fan in the inner quarters and himself traded favors for appointments.
value.literal: Down to Shizu [1], he began personally selecting from good families; thereafter the emperor hid behind the silk fan and personally practiced solicitation.

value.zh: 后採長白，實彰妒忌之情；
value.en: An empress chosen for graying hair laid bare the spite of jealousy;
value.literal: The empress chose “long white,” truly displaying jealousy;

value.zh: 賈納短青，竟踐覆亡之轍。
value.en: the Jias welcomed a young rival and eventually followed the same rut to ruin.
value.literal: Jia took in “short green,” and in the end trod the rut of overthrow.

value.zh: 得失遺跡，煥在綈緗，興滅所由，義同畫一。
value.en: Success and failure still gleam from the silk-bound histories; the springs of fortune and disaster follow one clear pattern.
value.literal: Tracks of gain and loss shine forth on silk documents; the causes of rise and ruin share one uniform pattern in meaning.

value.zh: 故列其本事，以為后妃傳云。
value.en: I therefore set out the essential facts as this “Treatise on Empresses and Consorts.”
value.literal: Therefore I array their basic affairs to form this treatise on empresses and consorts.

value.zh: 后暴戾日甚。
value.en: Her cruelty mounted daily.
value.literal: Consort violent cruelty daily worsened.

value.zh: 侍中賈模，后之族兄，右衛郭彰，后之從舅，並以才望居位，與楚王瑋、東安公繇分掌朝政。
value.en: Jia Mo and Guo Zhang ran court beside Sima Wei and Sima Yao.
value.literal: Palace Attendant Jia Mo—consort’s lineage elder; Guards-general Guo Zhang—consort’s maternal uncle—both by talent and prestige held posts sharing governance with Prince Chu Wei and Duke Dongan Yao.

value.zh: 后母廣城君養孫賈謐干預國事，權侔人主。
value.en: Lady Guo raised Jia Mi—his power rivaled the throne.
value.literal: Consort mother Lady Guangcheng raised grandson Jia Mi meddling state affairs—authority matched sovereign.

value.zh: 繇密欲廢后，賈氏憚之。
value.en: Sima Yao plotted deposition—Jias feared him.
value.literal: Yao secretly wished depose consort—Jia faction feared him.

value.zh: 及太宰亮、衛瓘等表繇徙帶方，奪楚王中候，后知瑋怨之，乃使帝作密詔令瑋誅瓘、亮，以報宿憾。
value.en: When Sima Liang and Wei Guan banished Yao and clipped Wei’s guard—she forged orders for Sima Wei to murder Liang and Wei.
value.literal: When Grand Mentor Liang and Wei Guan memorialized to exile Yao to Daifang and strip Prince Chu of central army inspector—consort knew Wei bore grudge—had emperor forge secret edict ordering Wei to kill Guan and Liang—settling old hatred.

value.zh: 模知后凶暴，恐禍及己，乃與裴頠、王衍謀廢之，衍悔而謀寢。
value.en: Jia Mo saw danger—planned coup with Pei Yi—Wang Yan backed out.
value.literal: Mo knew consort fierce—feared disaster reaching himself—with Pei Yi and Wang Yan plotted deposition—Yan repented—plot slept.

value.zh: 元敬虞皇后
value.en: Empress Yu, posthumously titled Respectful and Reverent.
value.literal: Empress Yu the Yuanjing (Primordial Reverence).

value.zh: 孝武帝立，寧康二年，以后母裴氏為廣德縣君。
value.en: After Emperor Xiaowu ascended the throne, he titled the empress's mother, Lady Pei, Mistress of Guangde county in the second year of Ningkang.
value.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu was established, in the second year of Ningkang he made the empress's mother the Lady Pei Mistress of Guangde county.

value.zh: 裴氏名穆，長水校尉綽孫，太傅主簿遐女，太尉王夷甫外孫。
value.en: Lady Pei was named Mu—granddaughter of the Colonel of the Chang River Guard Pei Chuo, daughter of the Grand Tutor's registrar Pei Xia, and maternal granddaughter of Grand Commandant Wang Yan.
value.literal: The Lady Pei had the name Mu; she was granddaughter of the Colonel of the Chang River Guard Chuo, daughter of the Registrar of the Grand Tutor Xia, and maternal granddaughter of Grand Commandant Wang Yan.

value.zh: 中表之美，高於當世。
value.en: Among her kin she stood out as one of the finest women of her generation.
value.literal: The beauty among cousins was higher than in the contemporary age.

value.zh: 遐隨東海王越遇害，無子。
value.en: Pei Xia had followed Sima Yue, Prince of Donghai, and was killed in the turmoil; he left no sons.
value.literal: Xia followed the Prince of Donghai Yue and encountered harm and died; he had no sons.

value.zh: 唯穆渡江，遂享榮慶，立第南掖門外，世所謂杜姥宅云。
value.en: Only Lady Mu escaped south across the Yangzi and lived to see honor and ease; she built a mansion outside the southern side gate—the house later known as Old Lady Du's.
value.literal: Only Mu crossed the Yangzi and thereupon enjoyed glory and felicity, erecting a mansion outside the southern Ye Gate—what the world calls Old Lady Du's house.

value.zh: 愍懷太子
value.en: Crown Prince Minhuai
value.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai

value.zh: 太子性剛，知賈謐恃後之貴，不能假借之。
value.en: Yu refused to flatter Jia Mi.
value.literal: The crown prince's temper was stiff; knowing Jia Mi relied on the empress's power, he would not indulge him.

value.zh: 謐至東宮，或舍之而於後庭遊戲。
value.en: He left Jia Mi cooling heels while he played inside.
value.literal: When Mi came to the Eastern Palace he sometimes left him waiting while he played in the inner courts.

value.zh: 詹事裴權諫曰：「賈謐甚有寵于中宮，而有不順之色，若一旦交構，大事去矣。
value.en: Household Superintendent Pei Quan remonstrated: "Jia Mi is deeply favored in the inner palace yet shows disrespectful looks—if they ever turn on you, the great enterprise is lost.
value.literal: Household Superintendent Pei Quan remonstrated: 'Jia Mi is deeply favored in the inner palace yet shows disrespectful looks—if they ever turn on you, the great enterprise is lost.

value.zh: 宜深自謙屈，以防其變，廣延賢士，用自輔翼。」
value.en: You should humble yourself deeply to guard against change and broadly recruit worthy men to aid your wings."
value.literal: You should humble yourself deeply to guard against change and broadly recruit worthy men to aid your wings.'

value.zh: 太子不能從。
value.en: Yu ignored him.
value.literal: The crown prince would not follow.

value.zh: 初，賈后母郭槐欲以韓壽女為太子妃，太子亦欲婚韓氏以自固。
value.en: Guo Huai once pushed a Han match—Yu wanted it too.
value.literal: Earlier Empress Jia's mother Guo Huai had wished to take Han Shou's daughter as crown princess; the crown prince also wished to marry the Hans to strengthen himself.

value.zh: 而壽妻賈午及後皆不聽，而為太子聘王衍小女惠風。
value.en: Jia Wu and the empress forced Wang Yan's younger daughter Huifeng instead.
value.literal: But Han Shou's wife Jia Wu and the empress both refused and instead betrothed the crown prince to Wang Yan's younger daughter Huifeng.

value.zh: 太子聞衍長女美，而賈后為謐聘之，心不能平，頗以為言。
value.en: Yu resented losing Wang's elder beauty to Jia Mi.
value.literal: The crown prince heard Wang's elder daughter was beautiful while the empress betrothed her to Jia Mi; his heart could not rest easy and he spoke of it often.

value.zh: 謐嘗與太子圍棋，爭道，成都王穎見而訶謐，謐意愈不平，因此譖太子于後曰：「太子廣買田業，多畜私財以結小人者，為賈氏故也。
value.en: Once while playing go with the crown prince Mi quarreled over a move; Ying, Prince of Chengdu, saw and rebuked Mi; Mi grew more resentful and slandered the crown prince to the empress: "The crown prince buys fields wholesale, hoards private wealth, and courts petty men—all because of the Jia clan.
value.literal: Once Mi played go with the crown prince and they quarreled over the move; Ying, Prince of Chengdu, saw and rebuked Mi; Mi grew more resentful and therefore slandered the crown prince to the empress: 'The crown prince buys fields wholesale, hoards private wealth, and courts petty men—all because of the Jia clan.

value.zh: 密聞其言云：'皇后萬歲後，吾當魚肉之。
value.en: Mi quoted Yu vowing to slaughter the Jias after Jia died.
value.literal: I have secretly heard him say: "After the empress dies, I shall butcher them."

value.zh: '非但如是也，若宮車晏駕，彼居大位，依楊氏故事，誅臣等而廢後於金墉，如反手耳。
value.en: Not only that—if the imperial carriage halts and he reaches the great seat, following Lady Yang's precedent he will execute us ministers and lock you away at Jinyong like turning his hand.
value.literal: Not only that—if the imperial carriage halts and he reaches the great seat, following Lady Yang's precedent he will execute us ministers and lock you away at Jinyong like turning his hand.

value.zh: 不如早為之所，更立慈順者以自防衛。」
value.en: Better strike early, remove him, and set up someone kindly and tractable to defend ourselves."
value.literal: Better strike early, remove him, and set up someone kindly and tractable to defend ourselves.'

value.zh: 後納其言，又宣揚太子之短，布諸遠近。
value.en: Jia adopted the plot and smeared Yu empire-wide.
value.literal: The empress accepted his words and further broadcast the crown prince's faults throughout near and far.

value.zh: 于時朝野咸知賈后有害太子意。
value.en: Everyone saw Jia meant to kill the heir.
value.literal: Then court and countryside knew the empress meant to harm the crown prince.

value.zh: 中護軍趙俊請太子廢後，太子不聽。
value.en: Zhao Jun urged preemptive deposition—Yu declined.
value.literal: Central Guard Zhao Jun asked the crown prince to depose the empress first; the crown prince refused.

value.zh: 初，太子之廢也，妃父王衍表請離婚。
value.en: Wang Yan filed for divorce the moment Yu fell.
value.literal: When the crown prince was first deposed, his father-in-law Wang Yan memorialized requesting divorce.

value.zh: 太子至許，遺妃書曰：「鄙雖頑愚，心念為善，欲盡忠孝之節，無有惡逆之心。
value.en: After reaching Xu he sent his consort a letter: "Though I am coarse and foolish, at heart I wished to do good and fulfill loyalty and filial piety—I harbored no rebellious evil.
value.literal: After the crown prince reached Xu he sent his consort a letter: 'Though I am coarse and foolish at heart I wished to do good and fulfill loyalty and filial piety—I harbored no rebellious evil.

value.zh: 雖非中宮所生，奉事有如親母。
value.en: He claimed dutiful service to Jia despite birth.
value.literal: Though not born of the inner palace I served her as my own mother.

value.zh: 自為太子以來，敕見禁檢，不得見母。
value.en: Palace rules barred him from Lady Xie.
value.literal: Since becoming crown prince edicts confined me—I could not see my mother.

value.zh: 自宜城君亡，不見存恤，恆在空室中坐。
value.en: Since the Lady of Yicheng died I received no comforting word—I constantly sat alone in empty rooms.
value.literal: Since the Lady of Yicheng died I received no comforting word—I constantly sat alone in empty rooms.

value.zh: 去年十二月，道文疾病困篤，父子之情，實相憐湣。
value.en: Last twelfth month Daowen became gravely ill; the affection between father and son made us deeply pity one another.
value.literal: Last twelfth month Daowen's illness grew desperate—father and son pitied each other truly.

value.zh: 于時表國家乞加徽號，不見聽許。
value.en: His plea for son's title failed.
value.literal: Then I petitioned the throne for honors—permission never came.

value.zh: 疾病既篤，為之求請恩福，無有噁心。
value.en: He denied malice in praying for the boy.
value.literal: When illness grew grave I sought blessings for him—I bore no evil intent.

value.zh: 自道文病，中宮三遣左右來視，云：'天教呼汝。
value.en: Since Daowen fell ill, the empress sent attendants three times to see me, saying, "His Majesty summons you."
value.literal: Since Daowen fell ill, the empress sent attendants three times to see me, saying, "His Majesty summons you."

value.zh: '到二十八日暮，有短函來，題言東宮發，疏云：'言天教欲見汝。
value.en: On the evening of the twenty-eighth a short letter arrived, marked as a dispatch from the Eastern Palace. It said, "His Majesty wishes to see you."
value.literal: On the evening of the twenty-eighth a short letter arrived, marked as a dispatch from the Eastern Palace. It said, "His Majesty wishes to see you."

value.zh: '即便作表求入。
value.en: He requested audience.
value.literal: At once I drafted a memorial begging entry.

value.zh: 二十九日早入見國家，須臾遣至中宮。
value.en: He saw Hui briefly then reached Jia's halls.
value.literal: On the twenty-ninth morning I entered and saw His Majesty; presently I was sent to the inner palace.

value.zh: 中宮左右陳舞見語：'中宮旦來吐不快。
value.en: Chen Wu claimed Jia was sick.
value.literal: Inner attendants Chen Wu told him: 'The empress vomited ill this morning.'

value.zh: '使住空屋中坐。
value.en: They parked him in an empty room.
value.literal: She told you to wait seated in an empty chamber.

value.zh: 須臾中宮遣陳舞見語：'聞汝表陛下為道文乞王，不得王是成國耳。
value.en: Presently the empress sent Chen Wu to tell me: 'I hear you petitioned His Majesty to make Daowen a prince and were refused. A princely title means a territorial domain, after all.'
value.literal: Presently the empress sent Chen Wu to tell me: 'I hear you petitioned His Majesty to make Daowen a prince and were refused. A princely title means a territorial domain, after all.'

value.zh: '中宮遙呼陳舞：'昨天教與太子酒棗。
value.en: The empress called to Chen Wu from a distance: "Yesterday His Majesty ordered wine and jujubes for the crown prince."
value.literal: The empress called to Chen Wu from a distance: "Yesterday His Majesty ordered wine and jujubes for the crown prince."

value.zh: '便持三升酒、大盤棗來見與，使飲酒啖棗盡。
value.en: Chen Wu forced three sheng wine and dates.
value.literal: She brought three sheng of ale and a great tray of jujubes and made him finish both.

value.zh: 鄙素不飲酒，即便遣舞啟說不堪三升之意。
value.en: Yu pleaded low tolerance.
value.literal: I never drink ale yet sent Chen Wu back explaining I could not manage three sheng.

value.zh: 中宮遙呼曰：'汝常陛下前持酒可喜，何以不飲？
value.en: The empress called from a distance: 'You are always so pleasing when you hold wine before His Majesty; why will you not drink?'
value.literal: The empress called from a distance: 'You are always so pleasing when you hold wine before His Majesty; why will you not drink?'

value.zh: 天與汝酒，當使道文差也。
value.en: His Majesty has given you wine; it should make Daowen recover.
value.literal: His Majesty has given you wine; it should make Daowen recover.

value.zh: '便答中宮：'陛下會同一日見賜，故不敢辭，通日不飲三升酒也。
value.en: Yu cited earlier imperial banquet.
value.literal: I answered the inner palace: His Majesty granted ale one day—therefore I dared not refuse—but all day I never drank three sheng.

value.zh: 且實未食，恐不堪。
value.en: Empty stomach worried him.
value.literal: Moreover I had not eaten—I feared I could not endure it.

value.zh: 又未見殿下，飲此或至顛倒。
value.en: Besides, I had not yet seen Your Highness, and drinking this might leave me confused and unsteady.
value.literal: Nor had I yet seen Your Highness—I feared drink might overturn me.

value.zh: '陳舞復傳語云：'不孝那！
value.en: Chen Wu called him unfilial.
value.literal: Chen Wu relayed another message: "You unfilial wretch!

value.zh: 天與汝酒飲，不肯飲，中有惡物邪？
value.en: His Majesty gives you wine to drink, yet you refuse. Is there something harmful in it?
value.literal: His Majesty gives you wine to drink, yet you refuse. Is there something harmful in it?

value.zh: '遂可飲二升，餘有一升，求持還東宮飲盡。
value.en: I then managed to drink two sheng. With one sheng left, I asked to take it back to the Eastern Palace and finish it there.
value.literal: I then managed to drink two sheng. With one sheng left, I asked to take it back to the Eastern Palace and finish it there.

value.zh: 逼迫不得已，更飲一升。
value.en: Cornered he drank more.
value.literal: Pressed helplessly he drank another sheng.

value.zh: 飲已，體中荒迷，不復自覺。
value.en: After drinking it, I became dazed and lost awareness.
value.literal: After drinking his body grew confused and he lost awareness.

value.zh: 須臾有一小婢持封箱來，云：'詔使寫此文書。
value.en: Presently a young maid brought a sealed case and said, "The emperor orders you to copy this document."
value.literal: Presently a young maid brought a sealed case, saying, 'The edict orders you to write out this document.'

value.zh: '鄙便驚起，視之，有一白紙，一青紙。
value.en: He found white and green paper inside.
value.literal: I started in alarm and looked: there was one sheet of white paper and one of green.

value.zh: 催促云：'陛下停待。
value.en: Runners said the emperor waited.
value.literal: They pressed: 'His Majesty is waiting.'

value.zh: '又小婢承福持筆研墨黃紙來，使寫。
value.en: Chengfu added brush and yellow paper for the copy.
value.literal: Another small maid, Chengfu, brought brush, inkstone, and yellow paper, making him write.

value.zh: 急疾不容復視，實不覺紙上語輕重。
value.en: Rush left no time to read the forgery's sense.
value.literal: Haste would not let me reread; I truly did not notice the import of the words on the page.

value.zh: 父母至親，實不相疑，事理如此，實為見誣，想眾人見明也。」
value.en: Parents are kin closest of all—I truly did not doubt them; though matters went so, I have been slandered, and I trust the multitude will see it clear.'
value.literal: Parents are kin closest of all—I truly did not doubt them; though matters went so, I have been slandered, and I trust the multitude will see it clear.'

value.zh: 順宗至德大聖大安孝皇帝諱誦，德宗長子，母昭德皇后王氏。
value.en: Shunzong, the Filial Emperor Song, was Dezong's eldest son; his mother was Empress Zhaode Wang.
value.literal: Emperor Shunzong, posthumous title To the Utmost Virtue Great Sage Great Peace Filial, taboo name Song, eldest son of Dezong; mother Empress Zhaode, née Wang.

value.zh: 上元二年正月生於長安之東內。
value.en: He was born in the eastern palace quarter of Chang'an in Shangyuan 2.
value.literal: In the first month of Shangyuan 2 he was born in the Eastern Inner Palace at Chang'an.

value.zh: 大曆十四年六月，封宣王。
value.en: In Dali 14 he received the title Prince of Xuan.
value.literal: In the sixth month of Dali 14 he was enfeoffed Prince of Xuan.

value.zh: 建中元年正月丁卯，立為皇太子。
value.en: He became crown prince on dingmao in the first month of Jianzhong 1.
value.literal: In the first month of Jianzhong 1, on dingmao, he was installed as heir apparent.

value.zh: 三月乙丑朔。
value.en: The third month opened on yichou.
value.literal: Third month, yichou new moon.

value.zh: 戊辰，詔常參官寒食拜墓，在畿內聽假日往還，他州府奏取進止。
value.en: Cold Food grave visits were regulated for capital officials on wuchen.
value.literal: On wuchen an edict: regular-attendance officials may visit graves at Cold Food — within the capital circuit they are permitted holiday travel back and forth; other prefectures and circuits memorialized for decision.

value.zh: 辛未，御史中丞武元衡奏：「中書門下御史台五品已上官、尚書省四品已上、諸司正三品已上、從三品職事官、東都留守、轉運鹽鐵節度觀察使、團練防禦招討經略等使、河南尹、同華州刺史、諸衛將軍三品已上官除授，皆入合謝，其餘官許于宣政南班拜訖便退。」
value.en: On xinwei Wu Yuanheng, vice censor-in-chief, memorialized: "Officials of the Secretariat-Chancellery and Censorate of fifth rank and above, the Department of State Affairs of fourth rank and above, all offices of full third rank and above, acting officials of the third rank, the eastern capital defender, transport and salt-and-iron commissioners, military, observation, training, defense, punitive, and strategy commissioners, the prefect of Henan, the prefects of Tongzhou and Huazhou, and generals of the guards of third rank and above shall all enter the hall to give thanks when appointed. The remaining officials may bow in the southern row at Xuanzheng and then withdraw."
value.literal: On xinwei Vice Censor-in-Chief Wu Yuanheng memorialized: "Officials of the Secretariat-Chancellery and Censorate of fifth rank and above, the Department of State Affairs of fourth rank and above, all regular third rank and above, acting third rank and above, eastern capital regent, transport and salt commissioners, military observation commissioners, defense and campaign commissioners, Governor of Henan, Governors of Tong and Hua, generals of the guards of third rank and above — on appointment all enter the hall to give thanks; other officials are permitted to bow at the southern court of Xuanzheng and withdraw."

value.zh: 詔曰：「如此例中有加使及職掌並准此。」
value.en: An edict said: "Where this precedent includes added commissioners and duties, all follow this."
value.literal: An edict said: "Where this precedent includes added commissioners and duties, all follow this."

value.zh: 又「兵部、吏部、禮部貢院官員，每舉選限內，有十月至二月不奉朝參。
value.en: Also: "Personnel of the War, Personnel, and Rites examination bureaus — within each selection limit, from the tenth month to the second month do not attend court.
value.literal: Also: "Personnel of the War, Personnel, and Rites examination bureaus — within each selection limit, from the tenth month to the second month do not attend court.

value.zh: 若稱事繁，則中書門下、御史台、度支、京兆府公事至重，朝謁如常。
value.en: If they claim affairs are numerous, then the Secretariat-Chancellery, Censorate, revenue office, and metropolitan government have affairs to the utmost — court attendance as usual.
value.literal: If they claim affairs are numerous, then the Secretariat-Chancellery, Censorate, revenue office, and metropolitan government have affairs to the utmost — court attendance as usual.

value.zh: 況旬節已賜歸休，又許分日，一月之內，才奉十日朝參，甚暑甚寒，又蒙矜放。
value.en: Moreover seasonal holidays already grant return rest, and divided days are also permitted — within one month they attend court only ten days; in great heat and great cold they are also shown compassion.
value.literal: Moreover seasonal holidays already grant return rest, and divided days are also permitted — within one month they attend court only ten days; in great heat and great cold they are also shown compassion.

value.zh: 臣求故實，以為王顏任中丞日嘗論其事，舉對甚詳。
value.en: Your subject seeks former precedent and holds that when Wang Yan held the censorate he once discussed this matter and answered in great detail.
value.literal: Your subject seeks former precedent and holds that when Wang Yan held the censorate he once discussed this matter and answered in great detail.

value.zh: 伏請准貞元十二年四月二十七日敕，永為常式。」
value.en: I humbly ask that the edict of Zhenyuan 12, fourth month, twenty-seventh day, be followed forever as constant form."
value.literal: I humbly ask that the edict of Zhenyuan 12, fourth month, twenty-seventh day, be followed forever as constant form."

value.zh: 從之。
value.en: The throne agreed.
value.literal: It was followed.

value.zh: 丙子，嚴礪收梓州。
value.en: Yan Li took Zizhou on bingzi.
value.literal: On bingzi Yan Li recovered Zizhou.

value.zh: 丁丑，制削奪劉辟在身官爵。
value.en: Liu Pi was stripped of rank on dingchou.
value.literal: On dingchou an order stripped Liu Pi of all offices held in life.

value.zh: 先是韓全義入朝，令其甥楊惠琳知留後，俄有詔除李演為節度，代全義。
value.en: Han Quanyi's nephew Yang Huilin had held the command until Li Yan was appointed.
value.literal: Earlier Han Quanyi entered court; he ordered his nephew Yang Huilin to act as regent; soon an edict appointed Li Yan military commissioner in his stead.

value.zh: 演赴任，惠琳據城叛，詔發河東、天德兵誅之。
value.en: Yang Huilin rebelled when Li Yan arrived; imperial troops were sent.
value.literal: Yan went to his post; Huilin held the city in rebellion; an edict sent Hedong and Tiande troops to execute him.

value.zh: 辛巳，夏州兵馬使張承金斬惠琳，傳首以獻。
value.en: Zhang Chengjin killed Huilin and presented his head on xinsi.
value.literal: On xinsi Xiazhou army commander Zhang Chengjin beheaded Huilin and sent the head as tribute.

value.zh: 壬辰，大行太上皇德妃董氏卒。
value.en: Lady Dong, Shunzong's consort, died on renchen.
value.literal: On renchen the late Retired Emperor's Virtuous Consort Lady Dong died.

value.zh: 以右神策行營節度高崇文檢校兵部尚書、梓州刺史、劍南東川節度。
value.en: Gao Chongwen, military commissioner of the Right Divine Strategy field command, was made acting minister of war, prefect of Zizhou, and military commissioner of Jiannan East.
value.literal: Gao Chongwen, military commissioner of the Right Divine Strategy field command, was made acting minister of war, prefect of Zizhou, and military commissioner of Jiannan East.

value.zh: 戊戌，以安南經略副使張舟為安南都護、本管經略使。
value.en: Zhang Zhou took Annan on wuxu.
value.literal: On wuxu Zhang Zhou, Annan pacification vice commissioner, was made Protector-General of Annan and circuit commissioner.

value.zh: 己亥，以前劍南東川節度使韋丹為晉絳觀察使。
value.en: Wei Dan went to the Jin-He circuit on jihai.
value.literal: On jihai former eastern Sichuan military commissioner Wei Dan was made Jin-He observer.

value.zh: 壬寅，以前安南經略使趙昌為廣州刺史、嶺南節度使。
value.en: On renyin Zhao Chang, former strategy commissioner of Annan, was made prefect of Guangzhou and military commissioner of Lingnan.
value.literal: On renyin Zhao Chang, former strategy commissioner of Annan, was made prefect of Guangzhou and military commissioner of Lingnan.

value.zh: 癸卯，前嶺南節度使徐申卒。
value.en: Xu Shen died on guimao.
value.literal: On guimao former Lingnan military commissioner Xu Shen died.

value.zh: 丙午，命宰臣監試製舉人于尚書省，以制舉人先朝所征，不欲親試也。
value.en: Ministers supervised the decree exam rather than the emperor on bingwu.
value.literal: On bingwu the councillors were ordered to supervise examination of decree-examination candidates at the Department of State Affairs — because decree candidates were summoned by the former dynasty and he did not wish to examine personally.

value.zh: 丁未，以檢校司空、平章事杜祐為司徒，所司備禮冊拜，平章事如故；
value.en: Du You became Minister of Education on dingwei while keeping the council;
value.literal: On dingwei Du You, acting Master of Works and Grand Councillor, was made Minister of Education; the relevant offices prepared rites for enfeoffment and bowing; Grand Councillor as before;

value.zh: 罷領度支、鹽鐵、轉運等使，從其讓也，仍以兵部侍即李巽代領其任。
value.en: he yielded fiscal posts to Li Xun.
value.literal: he ceased leading revenue, salt, iron, and transport commissions — following his declination — and Vice Minister of War Li Xun was still made to lead those duties.

value.zh: 戊申，以隴右經略使、秦州經略使、秦州刺史劉澭為保義軍節度使。
value.en: On wushen Liu Yong, strategy commissioner of Longyou and Qinzhou and prefect of Qinzhou, was made military commissioner of Baoyi Army.
value.literal: On wushen Liu Yong, strategy commissioner of Longyou and Qinzhou and prefect of Qinzhou, was made military commissioner of Baoyi Army.

value.zh: 賑浙東米十萬石。
value.en: Zhedong received famine relief grain.
value.literal: Zhedong was given 100,000 piculs of relief grain.

value.zh: 己未，武元衡奏，常參官兼御史大夫、中丞者，准檢校省官例，立在本品同類之上。
value.en: Wu Yuanheng fixed precedence for censor-concurrents on jiwei.
value.literal: On jiwei Wu Yuanheng memorialized: regular-attendance officials who are concurrent Censor-in-Chief or vice censor — follow the precedent for acting provincial officials, standing above others of the same original rank.

value.zh: 壬戌，邵王約薨。
value.en: Prince Yue of Shao died on renxu.
value.literal: On renxu Prince of Shao Yue died.

value.zh: 武元衡奏：「正衙待制官，本置此官以備問。
value.en: Wu Yuanheng memorialized: "Regular-attendance awaiting-order officials — originally this office was established to prepare for questioning.
value.literal: Wu Yuanheng memorialized: "Regular-attendance awaiting-order officials — originally this office was established to prepare for questioning.

value.zh: 比來正衙多不奏事。
value.en: Recently at regular court many do not present business.
value.literal: Recently at regular court many do not present business.

value.zh: 自今後請以尚書省六品以上職事官、東宮師傅賓詹、王傅等，每坐日令兩人待制，退朝，詔于延英候對。」
value.en: From now on let officials of the Department of State Affairs of sixth rank and above with substantive posts, eastern palace tutors, companions, and princes' tutors — each court day two await order; after court, order them to wait at Yanying for audience."
value.literal: From now on let officials of the Department of State Affairs of sixth rank and above with substantive posts, eastern palace tutors, companions, and princes' tutors — each court day two await order; after court, order them to wait at Yanying for audience."

value.zh: 從之。
value.en: The throne agreed.
value.literal: It was followed.

value.zh: 天福元年十一月己亥，帝御北京崇元殿，降制：「改長興七年為天福元年，大赦天下。
value.en: On the jihai day of the eleventh month of Tianfu 1, the emperor entered the Chongyuan Hall at the Northern Capital and promulgated an edict: "The seventh year of Changxing is hereby renamed Tianfu 1, and a general amnesty is proclaimed for all under Heaven.
value.literal: On the jihai day of the eleventh month of the first year of Tianfu, the Emperor took the throne in the Chongyuan Hall at the Northern Capital and issued an edict: "Let the seventh year of Changxing be changed to the first year of Tianfu, and grant a general amnesty throughout the realm.

value.zh: 十一月九日昧爽已前，應在京及諸州諸色罪犯，及曾授偽命職掌官吏，並見禁囚徒，已結正未結正，已發覺未發覺，罪無輕重，常赦不原者，咸赦除之。
value.en: Before dawn on the ninth day of the eleventh month, every class of offender in the capital and in the provinces, every official who had once held office under the usurper regime, and every prisoner still in custody—case closed or pending, offense known or not, grave or slight, including crimes ordinarily beyond the reach of amnesty—was pardoned and set free.
value.literal: Before dawn on the ninth day of the eleventh month, all offenders of every category in the capital and the various prefectures, officials who had once received appointments from the false regime, and prisoners currently held in custody—whether their cases had been concluded or not, whether discovered or not, regardless of the severity of the offense, and even those normally excluded from routine amnesties—were all pardoned and released.

value.zh: 應明宗朝所行敕命法制，仰所在遵行，不得改易。
value.en: The edicts and statutes issued in the Tang reign of Emperor Mingzong are to be observed everywhere as written, without change.
value.literal: As for the edicts and regulations promulgated in the reign of Emperor Mingzong of Tang, [authorities] in each locality are to follow them and may not alter them.

value.zh: 其在京鹽貨，元是官場出糴，自今後並不禁斷，一任人戶取便糴易，仍下太原府，更不得開場糴貨。
value.en: Salt in the capital had formerly been sold only through government markets; hereafter the trade is not to be restricted, and households may buy and sell freely. Taiyuan Prefecture was likewise ordered to cease operating state salt-purchase depots.
value.literal: Salt goods in the capital had originally been purchased from government depots; from now on this monopoly is not to be enforced, and households may buy and sell as they please; an order was also sent to Taiyuan Prefecture that it must no longer operate purchasing depots for salt.

value.zh: 其曲每斤與減價錢三十文。」
value.en: The price of distilled liquor was cut by thirty cash per jin."
value.literal: For liquor, the price per jin was to be reduced by thirty cash."

value.zh: 以節度判官趙瑩為翰林學士承旨、守尚書戶部侍郎、知河東軍府事，以節度掌書記桑維翰為翰林學士、守尚書禮部侍郎、知樞密院事，以觀察判官薛融為吏部郎中兼侍御史、知雜事，太原縣令羅周嶽為左諫議大夫，節度推官竇貞固為翰林學士，軍城都巡檢使劉知遠為侍衛馬軍都指揮使，客將景延廣為步軍都指揮使，太原少尹李玘為尚書工部侍郎。
value.en: Zhao Ying, judge of the military administration, was appointed Grand Academician and Drafter of the Hanlin Academy, acting Minister of Revenue, with charge of Hedong military prefecture affairs; Sang Weihan, military secretary, became Hanlin Academician, acting Minister of Rites, and Controller of the Bureau of Military Affairs; Xue Rong, observation judge, became Director in the Ministry of Personnel with concurrent Remonstrance Censor and supervising censor; Luo Zhouyue, magistrate of Taiyuan County, became Left Remonstrance Censor; Dou Zhengu, military evaluator, became Hanlin Academician; Liu Zhiyuan, chief metropolitan garrison inspector, became Commander of the Palace Guard Cavalry; Jing Yanguang, guest officer, became Commander of the Palace Guard Infantry; and Li Qi, vice magistrate of Taiyuan, became Vice Minister of Works.
value.literal: Zhao Ying, military administration judge, was made Grand Academician and Drafter of the Hanlin Academy, acting Minister of Revenue, and in charge of Hedong military prefecture affairs; Sang Weihan, military administration secretary, was made Hanlin Academician, acting Minister of Rites, and Controller of the Bureau of Military Affairs; Xue Rong, observation administration judge, was made Director in the Ministry of Personnel with concurrent Remonstrance Censor and chief supervising censor; Luo Zhouyue, magistrate of Taiyuan County, was made Left Remonstrance Censor; Dou Zhengu, military administration evaluator, was made Hanlin Academician; Liu Zhiyuan, metropolitan garrison chief inspector, was made Commander of the Palace Guard Cavalry; Jing Yanguang, guest officer, was made Commander of the Palace Guard Infantry; Li Qi, vice magistrate of Taiyuan, was made Vice Minister of Works.

value.zh: 夏五月壬子朔，帝御崇元殿受朝賀，仗衛如式。
value.en: On the first day of the fifth month the emperor received congratulations in the Chongyuan Hall with full ceremonial guard.
value.literal: On the first day of the fifth month of summer, renzi, the Emperor took the throne in the Chongyuan Hall to receive congratulatory homage, with guards and insignia in full form.

value.zh: 詔洛京、魏府管內所征今年夏苗稅麥等，宜放五分之一，以微旱故也。
value.en: Summer seedling taxes and wheat levies collected this year in the Luoyang capital and Weifu circuits were remitted by one-fifth because of slight drought.
value.literal: An edict stated that summer seedling taxes and wheat levies collected this year within the Luoyang capital and Weifu circuits should be remitted by one-fifth, because of slight drought.

value.zh: 丙辰，御史中丞張昭遠奏：「汴州在梁室朱氏稱制之年，有京都之號，及唐莊宗平定河南，復廢為宣武軍。
value.en: On the bingchen day, Censor-in-Chief Zhang Zhaoyuan memorialized: "Bianzhou, in the years when the Zhu clan of Liang held power, bore the title of capital; when Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong pacified Henan it was again abolished and made Xuanwu Army.
value.literal: On the bingchen day, Censor-in-Chief Zhang Zhaoyuan memorialized: "Bianzhou, in the years when the Zhu clan of Liang held power, bore the title of capital; when Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong pacified Henan it was again abolished and made Xuanwu Army.

value.zh: 至明宗行幸之時，掌事者因緣修葺衙城，遂掛梁室時宮殿門牌額，當時識者或竊非之。
value.en: When Emperor Mingzong toured, those in charge repaired the headquarters city and hung palace gate placards from Liang times—men of discernment privately disapproved.
value.literal: When Emperor Mingzong toured, those in charge took occasion to repair the headquarters city and hung palace gate placards from Liang times—men of discernment at the time privately disapproved.

value.zh: 一昨車駕省方，暫居梁苑，臣觀衙城內齋閣牌額，一如明宗行幸之時，無都號而有殿名，恐非典據。
value.en: When the emperor recently toured and temporarily resided in Liangyuan, I observed placards on pavilions within the headquarters city as in Mingzong's tour—no capital designation but hall names—and fear this is not canonical precedent.
value.literal: When the carriage recently toured the realm and temporarily resided in Liangyuan, your subject observed placards on pavilions within the headquarters city just as in Mingzong's tour—no capital designation but hall names—and fears this is not canonical precedent.

value.zh: 臣竊尋秦、漢已來，寰海之內，鑾輿所至，多立宮名。
value.en: Since Qin and Han, wherever the imperial carriage went within the realm, palace names were often established.
value.literal: Your subject has traced since Qin and Han that wherever the imperial carriage went within the realm, palace names were often established.

value.zh: 近代隋室於揚州立江都宮，太原立汾陽宮，岐州立仁壽宮。
value.en: In recent times the Sui established the Jiangdu Palace at Yangzhou, the Fenyang Palace at Taiyuan, and the Renshou Palace at Qizhou.
value.literal: In recent times the Sui house established the Jiangdu Palace at Yangzhou, the Fenyang Palace at Taiyuan, and the Renshou Palace at Qizhou.

value.zh: 唐朝於太原立晉陽宮，同州立長春宮，岐州立九成宮。
value.en: The Tang established the Jinyang Palace at Taiyuan, the Everlasting Spring Palace at Tongzhou, and the Ninefold Palace at Qizhou.
value.literal: The Tang house established the Jinyang Palace at Taiyuan, the Everlasting Spring Palace at Tongzhou, and the Ninefold Palace at Qizhou.

value.zh: 宮中殿閣，皆題署牌額，以類皇居。
value.en: Halls and pavilions within the palaces all bore inscribed placards, resembling the imperial residence.
value.literal: Halls and pavilions within the palaces all bore inscribed placards, resembling the imperial residence.

value.zh: 請準故事，於汴州衙城門權掛一宮門牌額，則其餘齋閣並可取便為名。」
value.en: We request following precedent to hang temporarily one palace gate placard at the Bianzhou headquarters gate; then the remaining pavilions may all be named as convenient."
value.literal: We request following precedent to hang temporarily one palace gate placard at the Bianzhou headquarters gate; then the remaining pavilions may all be named as convenient."

value.zh: 敕：行闕宜以大寧宮為名。
value.en: An edict named the traveling palace the Great Tranquility Palace.
value.literal: An edict: The traveling palace should be named the Great Tranquility Palace.

value.zh: 湖南青草廟舊封安流侯，進封廣利公；
value.en: The Green Grass Temple in Hunan, formerly Marquis of Anliu, was advanced to Duke of Guangli;
value.literal: The Green Grass Temple in Hunan, formerly enfeoffed as Marquis of Anliu, was advanced to Duke of Guangli;

value.zh: 洞庭廟進封靈濟公；
value.en: The Dongting Shrine was promoted to Duke Spirit-Benefit;
value.literal: The Dongting Shrine was advanced in title to Duke Spirit-Benefit;

value.zh: 磊石廟舊封昭靈侯，進封威顯公；
value.en: The Leishi Shrine, previously Marquis Splendid Spirit, was promoted to Duke Majestic Manifestation;
value.literal: The Leishi Shrine, formerly enfeoffed as Marquis Splendid Spirit, was advanced to Duke Majestic Manifestation;

value.zh: 黃陵二妃廟舊封懿節廟，改封昭烈廟，從馬希範之請也。
value.en: At Ma Xifan's request, the shrine of the Two Consorts at Huangling, formerly the Yi Jie Shrine, was retitled the Splendid Fierce Shrine.
value.literal: The shrine of the Two Consorts at Huangling, formerly titled the Yi Jie Shrine, was renamed the Splendid Fierce Shrine, in accordance with Ma Xifan's request.

value.zh: 戊午，以前成德軍節度判官張彭為太府卿。
value.en: On wuwu, Zhang Peng, former Chengde military administration judge, became Minister of the Imperial Treasury.
value.literal: On the wuwu day, Zhang Peng, formerly adjutant to the military governor of Chengde Circuit, was appointed Minister of the Imperial Treasury.

value.zh: 壬戌，詔在朝文武臣僚，每人各進封事一件。
value.en: On renxu the court decreed that every civil and military official in attendance submit one sealed memorial.
value.literal: On the renxu day, an edict ordered all civil and military officials at court to each submit one sealed memorial.

value.zh: 仍須實封通進，務裨闕政，用副虛懷。
value.en: Memorials were to be submitted under real seal, to remedy failings in government and answer the emperor's open-minded solicitude.
value.literal: They were also required to submit them fully sealed, striving to remedy governmental deficiencies, to match his humble receptivity.

value.zh: 甲子，以虞部郎中、知制誥於嶠為中書舍人，以戶部郎中於遘為虞部郎中、知制誥，故太子少保致仕朱漢賓贈司空。
value.en: On jiazi, Yu Qiao, Bureau Director in the Ministry of Works and rescript drafter, became Secretariat Drafter; Yu Hou, Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue, became Bureau Director in the Ministry of Works and rescript drafter; and the late retired Junior Guardian Zhu Hanbin was posthumously granted Sikong.
value.literal: On the jiazi day, Yu Qiao, Bureau Director in the Ministry of Works and drafter of edicts, was made Deputy Director of the Secretariat; Yu Hou, Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue, was made Bureau Director in the Ministry of Works and drafter of edicts; the late retired Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent Zhu Hanbin was posthumously granted Sikong.

value.zh: 乙丑，六宅使王繼宏送義州衙前收管，前洺州團練使高信送復州收管。
value.en: On yichou, Palace Attendant Wang Jihong was remanded to Yi prefectural custody, and former Mingzhou defensive commissioner Gao Xin to Fu prefecture.
value.literal: On the yichou day, Palace Attendant Wang Jihong was sent to be detained at the Yi prefectural yamen, and former Mingzhou defensive commissioner Gao Xin was sent to be detained at Fu prefecture.

value.zh: 二人於崇禮門內喧爭，為臺司所劾故也。
value.en: This was because they had quarreled noisily inside the Chongli Gate and had been impeached by the censorate.
value.literal: The reason was that the two men had quarreled loudly inside the Chongli Gate and had been impeached by the censorate.

value.zh: 戊辰，翰林學士、戶部員外郎、知制誥竇貞固改工部郎中、知制誥；
value.en: On wuchen, Hanlin Academician Dou Zhengu, Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue and rescript drafter, became Bureau Director in the Ministry of Works and rescript drafter;
value.literal: On the wuchen day, Hanlin Academician Dou Zhengu, Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue and drafter of edicts, was transferred to Bureau Director in the Ministry of Works and drafter of edicts;

value.zh: 翰林學士、都官郎中、知制誥李慎儀改中書舍人，仍賜金紫，並依舊充職。
value.en: Hanlin Academician Li Shenyi, Bureau Director in the Ministry of Justice and rescript drafter, became Secretariat Drafter, was again granted the gold seal and purple robe, and both men continued in their former capacities.
value.literal: Hanlin Academician Li Shenyi, Bureau Director in the Ministry of Justice and drafter of edicts, was transferred to Deputy Director of the Secretariat, and was still granted the gold seal and purple robe; both continued in their previous posts.

value.zh: 庚午，制封皇第二十一女為長安公主，封皇第十一妹烏氏為壽安長公主，皇第十二妹史氏為永壽長公主，皇第十三妹杜氏為樂平長公主。
value.en: On gengwu an edict enfeoffed the emperor's twenty-first daughter as Princess of Chang'an; his eleventh younger sister, Lady Wu, as Grand Princess of Shou'an; his twelfth younger sister, Lady Shi, as Grand Princess of Yongshou; and his thirteenth younger sister, Lady Du, as Grand Princess of Leping.
value.literal: On the gengwu day, by edict the emperor's twenty-first daughter was enfeoffed as Princess of Chang'an; the emperor's eleventh younger sister, Lady Wu, as Grand Princess of Shou'an; the twelfth younger sister, Lady Shi, as Grand Princess of Yongshou; and the thirteenth younger sister, Lady Du, as Grand Princess of Leping.

value.zh: 壬申，天雄軍節度使、守太傅、兼中書令、興唐尹範延光進封臨清王，加食邑三千戶；
value.en: On renshen, Fan Yanguang, Military Commissioner of Tianxiong, acting Grand Preceptor, Palace Secretariat Director, and Prefect of Xingtang, was promoted Prince of Linqing with an additional fief of three thousand households;
value.literal: On the renshen day, Fan Yanguang, Military Commissioner of Tianxiong Army, acting Grand Preceptor, concurrent Palace Secretariat Director, and Prefect of Xingtang, was advanced to Prince of Linqing, with an additional fief of three thousand households;

value.zh: 鳳翔節度使、檢校太師、兼中書令、西平王李從嚴進封岐王。
value.en: Li Congyan, Military Commissioner of Fengxiang, Acting Grand Mentor, Palace Secretariat Director, and Prince of Xiping, was promoted Prince of Qi.
value.literal: Li Congyan, Military Commissioner of Fengxiang, Acting Grand Mentor, concurrent Palace Secretariat Director, and Prince of Xiping, was advanced to Prince of Qi.

value.zh: 丙子，平盧軍節度使、兼中書令王建立進封臨淄王；
value.en: On bingzi, Wang Jianli, Military Commissioner of Pinglu and Palace Secretariat Director, was promoted Prince of Linzi;
value.literal: On the bingzi day, Wang Jianli, Military Commissioner of Pinglu Army and concurrent Palace Secretariat Director, was advanced to Prince of Linzi;

value.zh: 昭信軍節度使、侍衛馬軍都指揮使景延廣改寧江軍節度使，典軍如故。
value.en: Jing Yanguang, Military Commissioner of Zhaoxin and commander of the palace cavalry guard, became Military Commissioner of Ningjiang while continuing to command troops as before.
value.literal: Jing Yanguang, Military Commissioner of Zhaoxin and Commander of the Palace Guard Cavalry, was transferred to Military Commissioner of Ningjiang; he continued to command troops as before.

value.zh: 太常卿梁文矩奏定四廟謚號、廟號、陵號，太常少卿裴垣奏定四廟皇后追尊謚號，從之。
value.en: Minister of Rites Liang Wenju proposed posthumous titles, temple names, and tomb names for the four imperial temples; Vice Minister of Rites Pei Yuan proposed posthumous titles for the empresses honored there; both were approved.
value.literal: Minister of Rites Liang Wenju memorialized on fixing the posthumous titles, temple names, and tomb names for the four imperial temples; Vice Minister of Rites Pei Yuan memorialized on fixing the posthumous honorific titles for the empresses of the four temples; the court approved.

value.zh: 戊寅，以中書舍人、權知貢舉王延為御史中丞，以翰林學士、戶部侍郎、知制誥崔棁為兵部侍郎充承旨，以翰林學士承旨、兵部侍郎程遜為檢校禮部尚書、太常卿，以檢校吏部尚書、太常卿梁文矩為吏部尚書，以御史中丞張昭遠為戶部侍郎，以吏部尚書盧文紀為太子少傅。
value.en: On wuyin, Wang Yan, Secretariat Drafter and acting chief examiner, became Censor-in-Chief; Cui Zhi, Hanlin Academician, Vice Minister of Revenue, and rescript drafter, became Vice Minister of War and chief drafter; Cheng Xun, Hanlin chief drafter and Vice Minister of War, became Acting Minister of Rites and Minister of Rites; Liang Wenju became Minister of Personnel; Zhang Zhaoyuan became Vice Minister of Revenue; and Lu Wenji became Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.
value.literal: On the wuyin day, Wang Yan, Secretariat Drafter and acting chief examiner, was made Censor-in-Chief; Cui Zhi, Hanlin Academician, Vice Minister of Revenue, and drafter of edicts, was made Vice Minister of War and chief drafter; Cheng Xun, Hanlin Academician, chief drafter, and Vice Minister of War, was made Acting Minister of Rites and Minister of Rites; Liang Wenju, Acting Minister of Personnel and Minister of Rites, was made Minister of Personnel; Zhang Zhaoyuan, Censor-in-Chief, was made Vice Minister of Revenue; Lu Wenji, Minister of Personnel, was made Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.

value.zh: 己卯，詔太社內先收掌唐朝罪人首級等，宜令骨肉或先舊僚屬收葬，其喪葬儀註不得過制。
value.en: On jimao an edict ordered that severed heads of Tang convicts kept at the Altar of Earth be released to kin or former colleagues for burial, with funeral observances kept within proper bounds.
value.literal: On the jimao day, an edict stated that the severed heads of Tang dynasty convicts previously held at the Altar of Earth should be released to their kin or former colleagues for burial, and that funeral rites must not exceed proper form.

value.zh: 開運二年夏五月丙申朔，帝御崇元殿受朝，大赦天下。
value.en: In Kaiyun 2, on the first day bingshen of the fifth summer month, the emperor held court at Chongyuan Hall, received homage, and proclaimed a general amnesty.
value.literal: In the second year of Kaiyun, on the first day bingshen of the fifth summer month, the emperor took the throne at Chongyuan Hall to receive court homage and proclaimed a general amnesty for all under Heaven.

value.zh: 丁酉，以右衛上將軍馬萬為左金吾上將軍致仕。
value.en: On dingyou Ma Wan, General of the Right Guard, was retired as General of the Left Golden Chancellery.
value.literal: On dingyou, Ma Wan, General of the Right Guard, was made retired General of the Left Golden Chancellery.

value.zh: 戊戌，陜州節度使宋彥筠移鎮鄧州，澶州節度使何建移鎮河陽。
value.en: On wuxu Song Yanyun moved from Shaan to Deng Prefecture, and He Jian from Chan to Heyang.
value.literal: On wuxu, Song Yanyun, military commissioner of Shaan Prefecture, was transferred to Deng Prefecture, and He Jian, military commissioner of Chan Prefecture, was transferred to Heyang.

value.zh: 以左神武統軍潘環為澶州節度使，以宣徽北院使李彥韜遙領壽州節度使兼侍衛馬軍都指揮使，以滄州節度使田武遙領夔州節度使兼侍衛步軍都指揮使。
value.en: Pan Huan became commissioner of Chan; Li Yantao held Shou remotely while commanding the palace cavalry; Tian Wu held Kui remotely while commanding the palace infantry.
value.literal: Pan Huan, commander of the Left Divine Martial Army, was made military commissioner of Chan Prefecture; Li Yantao, commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, was given concurrent remote command of Shou Prefecture and made commander of the Palace Guards Cavalry; Tian Wu, military commissioner of Cang Prefecture, was given concurrent remote command of Kui Prefecture and made commander of the Palace Guards Infantry.

value.zh: 辛亥，白虹貫日。
value.en: On xinhai a white rainbow spanned the sun.
value.literal: On xinhai, a white rainbow pierced the sun.

value.zh: 壬子，宰臣桑維翰、劉句、李崧、和凝並加階爵。
value.en: On renzi chief ministers Sang Weihan, Liu Xu, Li Song, and He Ning all received higher ranks and fiefs.
value.literal: On renzi, the chief ministers Sang Weihan, Liu Xu, Li Song, and He Ning were all advanced in rank and enfeoffment.

value.zh: 禮部尚書竇貞固改刑部尚書，太常寺卿王松改工部尚書。
value.en: Dou Zhengu moved from Rites to Justice, and Wang Song from Ceremonies to Works.
value.literal: Dou Zhengu, Minister of Rites, was changed to Minister of Justice; Wang Song, Director of the Directorate of Ceremonies, was changed to Minister of Works.

value.zh: 以尚書左丞龍敏為太常卿；
value.en: Long Min, Left Vice Director of State Affairs, became Director of Ceremonies;
value.literal: Long Min, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, was made Director of Ceremonies;

value.zh: 以翰林學士承旨、兵部侍郎李慎儀為尚書左丞；
value.en: Li Shenyi, Hanlin chief academician and Vice Minister of War, became Left Vice Director of State Affairs;
value.literal: Li Shenyi, Hanlin Academician-in-Chief and Vice Minister of War, was made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs;

value.zh: 以御史中丞張允為兵部侍郎、知制誥，充翰林學士承旨；
value.en: Zhang Yun, Censor-in-Chief, became Vice Minister of War and drafter of rescripts and Hanlin chief academician;
value.literal: Zhang Yun, Censor-in-Chief, was made Vice Minister of War, drafter of imperial rescripts, and appointed Hanlin Academician-in-Chief;

value.zh: 以左諫議大夫顏衎為御史中丞；
value.en: Yan Kan, Left Remonstrance Counselor, became Censor-in-Chief;
value.literal: Yan Kan, Left Remonstrance Counselor, was made Censor-in-Chief;

value.zh: 〈（《宋史·顏衎傳》：喪亂之後，朝綱不振，衎執憲頗有風采，嘗上言：「才除御史者旋授外藩賓佐，復有以私故細事求假外拜，州郡無參謁之儀，出入失風憲之體，漸恐四方得以輕易，百辟無所準繩。
value.en: (Song History, biography of Yan Kan: After the civil wars court discipline had slackened; Kan enforced the law with notable vigor and once memorialized: "Newly appointed censors are immediately sent as staff to frontier prefectures, and others use petty private pretexts to leave the capital for provincial posts. Prefectures then lack proper audience protocol, and the censorate loses its dignity—soon the realm may hold it in contempt and officials will have no standard.
value.literal: (Biography of Yan Kan in the Song History: After the disorders, court discipline was slack; Kan in enforcing the law showed considerable authority and once memorialized: "Those just made censors are immediately appointed as staff to outer prefectures; moreover some seek leave for minor private matters to go out and take provincial posts, so that prefectures have no protocol for audiences, and coming and going lose the dignity proper to the censorate—gradually the four quarters may take things lightly and the hundred officials have no standard to follow.

value.zh: 請自今藩鎮幕僚，勿得任臺官；
value.en: Henceforth let prefectural staff not hold censorate posts;
value.literal: I request that from now on prefectural staff may not hold censorate posts;

value.zh: 雖親王宰相出鎮，亦不得奏充賓佐；
value.en: even when princes or chief ministers take field commands, they may not be named as staff;
value.literal: even when imperial princes or chief ministers go out to command prefectures, they may not be recommended as staff;

value.zh: 非奉制勘事，勿得出京；
value.en: and except on imperial commission to investigate, censors may not leave the capital;
value.literal: except on imperial commission to investigate matters, they may not leave the capital;

value.zh: 自余不令釐雜務。」
value.en: nor handle miscellaneous duties."
value.literal: as for the rest, do not allow them to take on miscellaneous duties."

value.zh: 詔惟辟召入幕，余從其請。）〉
value.en: The edict allowed only imperial summons to enter staffs; the rest was approved.)〉
value.literal: An edict allowed only those summoned by imperial appointment to enter staffs; the rest of his requests were approved.)〉

value.zh: 以兵部侍郎、宏文館學士、判館事田敏為國子祭酒；
value.en: Tian Min, Vice Minister of War and Hongwen academician, became Chancellor of the Directorate of Education;
value.literal: Tian Min, Vice Minister of War, academician of the Hongwen Hall, and overseer of the hall, was made Chancellor of the Directorate of Education;

value.zh: 以戶部侍郎段希堯為兵部侍郎；
value.en: Duan Xiyao, Vice Minister of Revenue, became Vice Minister of War;
value.literal: Duan Xiyao, Vice Minister of Revenue, was made Vice Minister of War;

value.zh: 以工部侍郎邊蔚為戶部侍郎，依前權知開封府事；
value.en: Bian Wei, Vice Minister of Works, became Vice Minister of Revenue while retaining acting charge of Kaifeng;
value.literal: Bian Wei, Vice Minister of Works, was made Vice Minister of Revenue and continued as before as acting overseer of Kaifeng Prefecture affairs;

value.zh: 以左散騎常侍李式為工部侍郎；
value.en: Li Shi, Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, became Vice Minister of Works;
value.literal: Li Shi, Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, was made Vice Minister of Works;

value.zh: 以給事中王仁裕為左散騎常侍。
value.en: Wang Renyu, Supervising Secretary, became Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry.
value.literal: Wang Renyu, Supervising Secretary, was made Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry.

value.zh: 甲寅，以華州節度使趙瑩為開封尹，以皇弟開封尹重睿為秦州節度使，以宣徽南院使劉繼勛為華州節度使，以前鄆州節度使張從恩為晉州節度使。
value.en: On jiayin Zhao Ying became Prefect of Kaifeng; the emperor's brother Chongrui left Kaifeng for Qin; Liu Jixun took Hua; and former Yun commissioner Zhang Cong'en took Jin.
value.literal: On jiayin, Zhao Ying, military commissioner of Hua Prefecture, was made Prefect of Kaifeng; the emperor's younger brother Chongrui, Prefect of Kaifeng, was made military commissioner of Qin Prefecture; Liu Jixun, commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, was made military commissioner of Hua Prefecture; Zhang Cong'en, former military commissioner of Yun Prefecture, was made military commissioner of Jin Prefecture.

value.zh: 丙辰，杜威來朝。
value.en: On bingchen Du Wei presented himself at court.
value.literal: On bingchen, Du Wei came to court.

value.zh: 定州奏，大風雹，北嶽廟殿宇樹木悉摧拔之。
value.en: Ding Prefecture reported that wind and hail had destroyed the halls and trees of the Northern Marchmount Temple.
value.literal: Ding Prefecture reported that a great wind and hail had utterly uprooted the halls and trees of the Northern Marchmount Temple.

value.zh: 七月壬辰，以禮部尚書王延為刑部尚書，以工部尚書王松為禮部尚書，以太常卿龍敏為工部尚書，以左丞李慎儀為太常卿，以吏部侍郎張昭遠為左丞，以右丞李詳為吏部侍郎，以前義州刺史李玘為右丞。
value.en: On renchen of the seventh month Wang Yan moved to Justice, Wang Song to Rites, Long Min to Works, Li Shenyi to Ceremonies, Zhang Zhaoyuan to Left Vice Director, Li Xiang to Civil Vice Minister, and former Yi prefect Li Qi to Right Vice Director.
value.literal: In the seventh month, on renchen, Wang Yan, Minister of Rites, was made Minister of Justice; Wang Song, Minister of Works, was made Minister of Rites; Long Min, Director of Ceremonies, was made Minister of Works; Li Shenyi, Left Vice Director, was made Director of Ceremonies; Zhang Zhaoyuan, Vice Minister of the Civil Office, was made Left Vice Director; Li Xiang, Right Vice Director, was made Vice Minister of the Civil Office; Li Qi, former prefect of Yi Prefecture, was made Right Vice Director.

value.zh: 前晉昌軍節度使安彥威薨，輟朝，贈太師。
value.en: Former Jinchang commissioner An Yanwei died; audiences were suspended and he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.
value.literal: An Yanwei, former military commissioner of the Jinchang Army, died; court audiences were suspended, and he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.

value.zh: 丙申，兩浙節度使、吳越國王錢宏佐加守太師，北京留守、河東節度使、北平王劉知遠加守太尉。
value.en: On bingshen Qian Hongzuo of Wuyue became Defender of Grand Preceptor and Liu Zhiyuan of Hedong Defender of Grand Marshal.
value.literal: On bingshen, Qian Hongzuo, military commissioner of the Two Zhes and King of Wuyue, was made Defender of Grand Preceptor; Liu Zhiyuan, garrison commander of the Northern Capital, military commissioner of Hedong, and Prince of Beiping, was made Defender of Grand Marshal.

value.zh: 滄州奏，蕃寇攻饒安縣。
value.en: Cang Prefecture reported barbarian forces attacking Rao'an County.
value.literal: Cang Prefecture reported that barbarian raiders were attacking Rao'an County.

value.zh: 楊劉口河決西岸，水闊四十里。
value.en: The Yellow River burst its west bank at Yangliu Ford; the flood spread forty li wide.
value.literal: The Yangliu Ford on the Yellow River burst its west bank; the water spread forty li wide.

value.zh: 以前鄧州節度使劉景巖為太子太師致仕。
value.en: Former Deng commissioner Liu Jingyan was retired as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
value.literal: Liu Jingyan, former military commissioner of Deng Prefecture, was made retired Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

value.zh: 辛亥，宋州谷熟縣河水雨水一概東流，漂沒秋稼。
value.en: On xinhai river and rain at Gushu in Song flowed east together and destroyed the autumn crop.
value.literal: On xinhai, in Gushu County of Song Prefecture, river water and rainwater alike flowed eastward and swept away the autumn grain.

value.zh: 丁巳，大理卿李專美卒。
value.en: On dingsi Li Zhuanmei, Director of Judicial Review, died.
value.literal: On dingsi, Li Zhuanmei, Director of the Court of Judicial Review, died.

value.zh: 戊午，詔偽清泰朝經削奪官爵朱宏昭、馮赟、康義誠、王思同、藥彥稠等，並復其官爵。
value.en: On wuwu an edict restored the ranks of Zhu Hongzhao, Feng Yun, Kang Yicheng, Wang Sitong, Yao Yanchou, and others stripped under the Qingtai reign.
value.literal: On wuwu, an edict restored the ranks and titles of Zhu Hongzhao, Feng Yun, Kang Yicheng, Wang Sitong, Yao Yanchou, and others, who under the false Qingtai reign had been stripped of office.

value.zh: 自夏初至是，河南、河北諸州郡餓死者數萬人，群盜蜂起，剽略縣鎮，霖雨不止，川澤泛漲，損害秋稼。
value.en: Since early summer Henan and Hebei had seen tens of thousands starve, bandits raid towns, endless rain flood the rivers, and the autumn crop ruined.
value.literal: From early summer until now, in the prefectures of Henan and Hebei tens of thousands died of hunger; bandits swarmed like bees, plundering counties and towns; unending rains made rivers and marshes overflow and harmed the autumn grain.

value.zh: 趙在禮，字翰臣，涿州人也。
value.en: Zhao Zaili, courtesy name Hanchen, was a native of Zhuozhou.
value.literal: Zhao Zaili, style name Hanchen, was a man of Zhuozhou.

value.zh: 曾祖景裕，祖士廉，皆不仕。
value.en: His great-grandfather Jingyu and grandfather Shilian both held no office.
value.literal: His great-grandfather Jingyu and grandfather Shilian both did not take office.

value.zh: 父元德，盧臺軍使。
value.en: His father Yuande served as military commissioner of the Lu Terrace.
value.literal: His father Yuande was Lu Terrace military commissioner.

value.zh: 在禮始事燕帥劉仁恭為小校，唐光化末，仁恭遣其子守文逐浮陽節度使盧彥威，據其城，升在禮為軍使，以佐守文。
value.en: Zaili first entered service under the Yan commander Liu Ren'gong as a junior officer. At the end of the Tang Guanghua era, Ren'gong sent his son Shouwen to expel Fuyang military commissioner Lu Yanwei and occupy his city, promoting Zaili to army commissioner to assist Shouwen.
value.literal: Zaili at first served the Yan commander Liu Ren'gong as a junior officer; at the end of the Guanghua era of Tang, Ren'gong sent his son Shouwen to drive out Fuyang military commissioner Lu Yanwei and seize his city, promoting Zaili to army commissioner to assist Shouwen.

value.zh: 及守文死，事其子。
value.en: After Shouwen died, he served his son in turn.
value.literal: When Shouwen died, he served his son.

value.zh: 延祚為守光所害，守光子繼威復為部將張萬進所殺，在禮遂事萬進。
value.en: Yanzuo was killed by Liu Shouguang; Shouguang's son Jiwei was in turn killed by the subordinate commander Zhang Wanjin, and Zaili then entered Wanjin's service.
value.literal: Yanzuo was killed by Shouguang; Shouguang's son Jiwei was again killed by the subordinate commander Zhang Wanjin, and Zaili then served Wanjin.

value.zh: 萬進奔梁，在禮乃與滄州留後毛璋歸太原。
value.en: When Wanjin fled to Liang, Zaili returned to Taiyuan together with Cangzhou acting prefect Mao Zhang.
value.literal: Wanjin fled to Liang; Zaili then together with Cangzhou acting prefect Mao Zhang returned to Taiyuan.

value.zh: 同光末，為效節指揮使，屯於貝州。
value.en: At the end of the Tongguang era he was commander of the Xiaojie army, stationed at Beizhou.
value.literal: At the end of Tongguang, he was Xiaojie army commander and was stationed at Beizhou.

value.zh: 會軍士皇甫暉等作亂，推指揮使楊晸為帥，晸不從，為眾所害，攜晸首以脅在禮。
value.en: When the soldiers Huangfu Hui and others mutinied, they tried to make the commander Yang Zheng their leader. Zheng refused and was killed by the mutineers, who then brought his head to force Zaili to lead them.
value.literal: It happened that the soldiers Huangfu Hui and others mutinied, pushing the commander Yang Zheng as leader; Zheng did not comply and was killed by the crowd, who carried Zheng's head to coerce Zaili.

value.zh: 在禮知其不可拒，遂從之，以四年二月六日引眾入鄴，在禮自稱留後。
value.en: Zaili knew he could not refuse, so he went along. On the sixth day of the second month of the fourth year he led his troops into Ye and styled himself acting prefect.
value.literal: Zaili knew it could not be refused, so he followed; on the sixth day of the second month in the fourth year he led the crowd into Ye, and Zaili styled himself acting prefect.

value.zh: 〈（《宋史·張錫傳》：趙在禮舉兵於鄴，瀕河諸州多構亂，錫權知棣州事，即出省錢賞軍，皆大悅，一郡獨全，棣人賴之。）〉
value.en: (The History of Song, biography of Zhang Xi, records that when Zhao Zaili raised troops at Ye, most of the prefectures along the river fell into disorder. Xi was acting prefect of Dizhou; he immediately paid out provincial funds to reward the troops, to general delight, and that prefecture alone remained secure—the people of Di were indebted to him.)〉
value.literal: (History of Song, Biography of Zhang Xi: When Zhao Zaili raised troops at Ye, the prefectures along the river for the most part stirred up disorder; Xi was acting prefect of Dizhou, immediately disbursed provincial funds to reward the army, all were greatly pleased, and that one prefecture alone remained intact—the people of Di relied on him.)〉

value.zh: 唐莊宗遣明宗率師討之，會城下軍亂，在禮迎明宗入城，事具《唐書》。
value.en: Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang sent Emperor Mingzong at the head of an army against him. When the troops below the walls mutinied, Zaili welcomed Mingzong into the city; the full account is in the Book of Tang.
value.literal: Tang Emperor Zhuangzong sent Mingzong at the head of an army to attack him; it happened that the army below the walls mutinied, and Zaili welcomed Mingzong into the city—the matter is fully set forth in the Book of Tang.

value.zh: 天成元年五月，授滑州節度使、檢校太保。
value.en: In the fifth month of the first year of Tiancheng he was appointed military commissioner of Huazhou and acting Grand Guardian.
value.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Tiancheng, he was appointed Huazhou military commissioner and acting Grand Guardian.

value.zh: 制下，在禮密奏軍情，未欲除移，且乞更伺少頃，尋就改天雄軍兵馬留後、鄴都留守、興唐尹。
value.en: When the appointment was announced, Zaili secretly reported on conditions in the army, saying he was not yet ready to be transferred and asking to wait a little longer. Soon afterward he was instead made acting commissioner of the Tianxiong army's horse and foot, garrison commander of the Ye capital, and prefect of Xingtang.
value.literal: When the edict was issued, Zaili secretly memorialized on military conditions, not yet wishing to be transferred, and moreover begged to wait a little longer; soon after he was changed to Tianxiong army acting commissioner of horse and foot, Ye capital garrison commander, and Xingtang prefect.

value.zh: 既而在禮將皇甫暉、趙進等相次除郡赴任，
value.en: Zaili then had Huangfu Hui, Zhao Jin, and others appointed in succession to prefectural posts and sent off to take office,
value.literal: Afterward Zaili had Huangfu Hui, Zhao Jin, and others in succession appointed to prefectures and sent to take up their posts,

value.zh: 〈（《歐陽史·皇甫暉傳》：明宗即位，暉自軍卒擢拜陳州刺史。
value.en: (Ouyang Xiu's history, biography of Huangfu Hui: When Emperor Mingzong took the throne, Hui was raised from the ranks to prefect of Chenzhou.
value.literal: (Ouyang's History, Biography of Huangfu Hui: When Mingzong took the throne, Hui was promoted from common soldier to Chenzhou prefect.

value.zh: 《九國誌·趙進傳》：天成初，除貝州刺史、鄴都衙內指揮使。）〉
value.en: Annals of the Nine States, biography of Zhao Jin: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was appointed prefect of Beizhou and commander of the Ye capital inner guard.)〉
value.literal: Annals of the Nine States, Biography of Zhao Jin: At the beginning of Tiancheng, he was made Beizhou prefect and Ye capital inner-palace army commander.)〉

value.zh: 在禮乃上表乞移旌節。
value.en: Zaili then memorialized, asking to be transferred to another post with full military commission.
value.literal: Zaili then submitted a memorial begging to be moved to another command with banners and staffs.

value.zh: 十二月，授滄州節度使。
value.en: In the twelfth month he was appointed military commissioner of Cangzhou.
value.literal: In the twelfth month, he was appointed Cangzhou military commissioner.

value.zh: 二年七月，移鎮兗州。
value.en: In the seventh month of the second year he was transferred to Yanzhou.
value.literal: In the seventh month of the second year, he was transferred to garrison Yanzhou.

value.zh: 長興元年，入為左驍衛上將軍，俄改同州節度使。
value.en: In the first year of Changxing he was recalled to the capital as General of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guards, and soon afterward was made military commissioner of Tongzhou.
value.literal: In the first year of Changxing, he entered the capital as General of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guards; soon after he was changed to Tongzhou military commissioner.

value.zh: 會高祖受明宗命統大軍伐蜀，以在禮充西川行營步軍都指揮使，收劍州而還。
value.en: When Gaozu received orders from Emperor Mingzong to command a great army against Shu, Zaili served as overall commander of the campaign's foot forces in the west, recovered Jianzhou, and returned.
value.literal: It happened that Gaozu received Mingzong's order to command a great army against Shu; Zaili was made overall commander of foot troops in the western Shu campaign headquarters, recovered Jianzhou, and returned.

value.zh: 四年，移鎮襄州。
value.en: In the fourth year he was transferred to Xiangzhou.
value.literal: In the fourth year, he was transferred to garrison Xiangzhou.

value.zh: 清泰三年，授宋州節度使，加檢校太尉、同平章事。
value.en: In the third year of Qingtai he was appointed military commissioner of Songzhou and given the additional titles of acting Grand Marshal and Grand Councillor.
value.literal: In the third year of Qingtai, he was appointed Songzhou military commissioner, with the added titles acting Grand Marshal and Fellow of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
