value.zh: 高祖登極，移鎮鄆州，加檢校太師、兼侍中，封衛國公。
value.en: When Gaozu took the throne, Zaili was transferred to Yunzhou, given the additional titles of acting Grand Preceptor and Palace Attendant, and enfeoffed as Duke of Wei.
value.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne, Zaili was transferred to garrison Yunzhou, with the added titles acting Grand Preceptor and Concurrent Palace Attendant, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Wei.

value.zh: 天福六年七月，授許州節度使。
value.en: In the seventh month of the sixth year of Tianfu he was appointed military commissioner of Xu Prefecture.
value.literal: In the seventh month of the sixth year of Tianfu, he was appointed military commissioner of Xu Prefecture.

value.zh: 八年四月，移鎮徐州，進封楚國公。
value.en: In the fourth month of the eighth year he was transferred to Xuzhou and advanced in rank to Duke of Chu.
value.literal: In the fourth month of the eighth year, he was transferred to garrison Xuzhou and advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Chu.

value.zh: 開運元年，以契丹為患，少帝議北征。
value.en: In the first year of Kaiyun, with the Khitan posing a threat, the Young Emperor considered a northern campaign.
value.literal: In the first year of Kaiyun, because the Khitan were a menace, the Young Emperor deliberated a northern expedition.

value.zh: 八月朔，降制命一十五將，以在禮為北面行營馬步都虞候。
value.en: On the first day of the eighth month, appointments were issued for fifteen generals; Zaili was made overall adjutant of horse and foot for the northern campaign.
value.literal: On the first day of the eighth month, edicts were issued appointing fifteen generals; Zaili was made overall adjutant of horse and foot in the northern campaign headquarters.

value.zh: 十一月，改行營副都統，都虞候如故。
value.en: In the eleventh month he was made deputy overall commander of the campaign, while retaining his post as overall adjutant.
value.literal: In the eleventh month, he was changed to deputy overall commander of the campaign headquarters, remaining overall adjutant as before.

value.zh: 受詔屯澶州，再除兗州節度使，依前副都統。
value.en: Ordered to encamp at Chanzhou, he was again appointed military commissioner of Yanzhou while continuing as deputy overall commander.
value.literal: He received orders to station at Chanzhou, was again appointed Yanzhou military commissioner, and continued as deputy overall commander as before.

value.zh: 三年正月，授晉昌軍節度使。
value.en: In the first month of the third year he was appointed military commissioner of the Jinchang army.
value.literal: In the first month of the third year, he was appointed Jinchang army military commissioner.

value.zh: 時少帝為其子延煦娶在禮女為妻，禮會之日，其儀甚盛，京師以為榮觀。
value.en: The Young Emperor had his son Yanxu marry Zaili's daughter. On the wedding day the ceremonies were splendid, and the capital treated the event as a spectacle of honor.
value.literal: At that time the Young Emperor took Zaili's daughter as wife for his son Yanxu; on the day of the ceremonial meeting the rites were very grand, and the capital regarded it as an occasion of glory to behold.

value.zh: 五月，進封秦國公，累食邑至一萬三千戶，實封一千五百戶。
value.en: In the fifth month he was advanced to Duke of Qin, with cumulative fief households rising to thirteen thousand and actual fief households of one thousand five hundred.
value.literal: In the fifth month, he was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Qin; his cumulative fief households reached thirteen thousand, with one thousand five hundred actual fief households.

value.zh: 張筠，海州人也。
value.en: Zhang Yun was a native of Haizhou.
value.literal: Zhang Yun, was a man of Haizhou.

value.zh: 父傳古，世為郡之大商，唐乾符末，屬江淮俶擾，遂徙家彭門。
value.en: His father Chuangu had for generations been one of the prefecture's great merchants. At the end of the Tang Qianfu era, with the Jiang-Huai region in turmoil, he moved the family to Pengmen.
value.literal: His father Chuangu was for generations a great merchant of the prefecture; at the end of the Qianfu era of Tang, because the Jiang-Huai region was in turmoil, he moved his household to Pengmen.

value.zh: 時彭門連帥時溥為東南面招討使，據有數郡之地，擢筠為偏將，累有軍功，奏授宿州刺史。
value.en: The Pengmen commander Shi Pu was then southeastern pacification commissioner, holding several prefectures. He promoted Yun to deputy general; Yun won repeated military distinction, and Pu memorialized to have him appointed prefect of Suzhou.
value.literal: At that time the Pengmen commander Shi Pu was southeastern pacification commissioner, holding several prefectures' territory; he promoted Yun to deputy general, who repeatedly had military merit, and memorialized to appoint him Suzhou prefect.

value.zh: 後溥與梁祖不協，梁人進攻宿州，下之，獲筠以歸。
value.en: Later, when Pu fell out with the Liang founder, Liang forces attacked Suzhou, captured it, and took Yun back with them.
value.literal: Later Pu was at odds with the Liang founder; Liang men advanced to attack Suzhou, took it, and captured Yun to bring back.

value.zh: 梁方圖霸業，以筠言貌辯秀，命為四鎮客將，久之，轉長直軍使。
value.en: With Liang then plotting supremacy, Yun's eloquence and polished appearance won him appointment as guest general of the four commands. After a long interval he was made chief of the long-duty army.
value.literal: Liang was then plotting hegemony; because Yun's speech and appearance were eloquent and refined, he was ordered to be a guest general of the four commands; after a long time he was transferred to chief of the long-duty army.

value.zh: 梁唐革命，遷右龍武統軍，歷客省使、宣徽使，出為復、商二州刺史，復為宣徽使。
value.en: When Liang gave way to Tang, Yun was transferred to commander of the Right Valiant Dragons, served in succession as guest-reception commissioner and palace treasury commissioner, was sent out as prefect of Fu and Shang, and again became palace treasury commissioner.
value.literal: When Liang underwent the Tang revolution, he was transferred to Right Valiant Dragon commander, served in succession as guest-reception commissioner and palace treasury commissioner, went out as prefect of Fu and Shang prefectures, and again became palace treasury commissioner.

value.zh: 梁室割相、衛為昭德軍，命筠為兩使留後。
value.en: The Liang court carved out Xiang and Wei as the Zhaode army and appointed Yun acting commissioner of both civil and military affairs.
value.literal: The Liang house carved Xiang and Wei into the Zhaode army and ordered Yun as acting commissioner of both civil and military affairs.

value.zh: 唐莊宗入魏，筠委城南歸，授右衛上將軍。
value.en: When Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang entered Wei, Yun abandoned the southern city and submitted, and was appointed General of the Right Guards.
value.literal: When Tang Emperor Zhuangzong entered Wei, Yun abandoned the southern city and returned, and was appointed General of the Right Guards.

value.zh: 會雍州康懷英以病告，詔筠往代之，比至，懷英已卒，因除筠為永平軍節度使、大安尹。
value.en: When Kang Huaiying of Yongzhou reported illness, Yun was ordered to replace him. By the time he arrived, Huaiying was already dead, and Yun was appointed military commissioner of the Yongping army and Intendant of Da'an.
value.literal: It happened that Yongzhou's Kang Huaiying reported illness; an edict ordered Yun to go replace him. By the time he arrived, Huaiying had already died, and Yun was therefore appointed Yongping army military commissioner and Da'an Intendant.

value.zh: 懷英在長安日，家財甚厚，筠盡奪之，復於大內掘地，繼獲金玉。
value.en: Huaiying had amassed great wealth while at Chang'an; Yun seized it all. He also dug within the inner palace grounds and unearthed gold and jade.
value.literal: When Huaiying was at Chang'an, his household wealth was very great; Yun seized it all. Again within the great inner palace he dug the ground and subsequently obtained gold and jade.

value.zh: 時有涇陽鎮將侯莫威，前與溫韜同剽唐氏諸陵，大貯瑰異之物，筠乃殺威而籍其家，遂蓄積巨萬。
value.en: The Jingyang garrison commander Hou Mowei had earlier joined Wen Tao in plundering the tombs of the Tang imperial house and hoarded extraordinary treasures. Yun killed him and confiscated his property, amassing wealth in the tens of thousands.
value.literal: At that time there was Jingyang garrison commander Hou Mowei, who earlier with Wen Tao together plundered the tombs of the Tang house and greatly stored rare and wondrous objects; Yun then killed Wei and registered his household, thereby amassing tens of thousands.

value.zh: 然性好施，每出遇貧民於路，則給與口食衣物，境內除省賦外，未嘗聚斂，遂致百姓不撓，十年小康，秦民懷惠，呼為「佛子」。
value.en: Yet he was generous by nature: whenever he went out and met the poor on the road, he gave them food and clothing. Apart from provincial levies, he never extorted within his jurisdiction, and the people were left unmolested. For ten years the region knew modest prosperity; the people of Qin were grateful and called him "the Buddha's son."
value.literal: Yet his nature was fond of giving; whenever he went out and met poor people on the road, he supplied them food and clothing. Within his jurisdiction, apart from provincial levies, he never amassed and exacted, and thereby caused the common people not to be harassed; for ten years there was modest prosperity, and the Qin people cherished his kindness, calling him "Buddha's Son."

value.zh: 同光中，從郭崇韜為劍南安撫使，蜀平歸洛，權領河南尹，俄鎮興元，所治之地，上下安之。
value.en: During the Tongguang era he followed Guo Chongtao as Jiannan pacification commissioner. After Shu was pacified he returned to Luoyang, served provisionally as Henan Intendant, and soon took up command at Xingyuan, where high and low alike lived in peace under his rule.
value.literal: In the Tongguang era, he followed Guo Chongtao as Jiannan pacification commissioner; when Shu was pacified he returned to Luoyang, provisionally headed Henan as Intendant, and soon garrisoned Xingyuan—the places he governed, high and low were at peace.

value.zh: 筠時有疾，軍州官吏久不得見，副使符彥琳等面請問疾，筠又不諾，彥琳等疑其已死，慮左右有謀，遂請權交牌印，筠命左右收彥琳下獄，以叛聞。
value.en: Yun was then ill, and the military and civil officials had long been unable to see him. Deputy commissioner Fu Yanlin and others came in person to inquire after his health, but Yun refused them again. Yanlin and the others suspected he was already dead and feared a plot among his attendants; they asked to take custody of the seals provisionally. Yun ordered his attendants to arrest Yanlin and imprison him, then reported him for rebellion.
value.literal: Yun at that time had illness; the army and prefecture officials for a long time could not see him. The deputy commissioner Fu Yanlin and others in person requested to inquire after his illness; Yun again did not assent. Yanlin and others suspected he was already dead and feared that those around him had designs; they therefore requested to hand over the tally and seal provisionally. Yun ordered those around him to seize Yanlin and put him in prison, reporting rebellion.

value.zh: 詔取彥琳等至洛，釋而不問，因授筠西京留守，誘離興元。
value.en: An edict summoned Yanlin and the others to Luoyang and released them without punishment. Yun was then appointed garrison commander of the western capital, a move intended to draw him away from Xingyuan.
value.literal: An edict took Yanlin and others to Luoyang, released them without inquiry, and thereby appointed Yun western capital garrison commander to lure him away from Xingyuan.

value.zh: 及至長安，守兵閉門不納，筠東朝於洛，詔遣歸第。
value.en: When he reached Chang'an, the garrison closed the gates and refused him entry. Yun went east to audience at Luoyang, where an edict sent him back to his private residence.
value.literal: When he reached Chang'an, the garrison troops closed the gates and would not admit him. Yun went east to audience at Luoyang; an edict sent him back to his residence.

value.zh: 筠前為京兆尹，奉詔殺偽蜀主王衍，衍之妓樂寶貨，悉私藏於家。
value.en: Yun had earlier served as Intendant of Jingzhao and, by imperial order, executed the puppet Shu ruler Wang Yan; he then secretly kept at home all of Yan's performers, music, and valuables.
value.literal: Previously, when Yun had been Intendant of Jingzhao, he received an edict to execute the false Shu ruler Wang Yan; Yan's entertainers, music, and treasures he secretly hoarded entirely at home.

value.zh: 及罷歸之後，第宅宏敞，花竹深邃，聲樂飲膳，恣其所欲，十年之內，人謂「地仙」。
value.en: After he retired and returned home, his mansion was grand and spacious, with deep groves of flowers and bamboo; music and feasting were at his pleasure. Within ten years people called him an "earth immortal."
value.literal: When he returned after leaving office, his residence was vast and spacious, flowers and bamboo deep and secluded, music and feasting as he wished; within ten years people called him an "earth immortal."

value.zh: 天福二年，上表乞歸長安，俄而洛下張從賓之亂，筠獨免其難，人咸謂筠有五福之具美焉。
value.en: In the second year of Tianfu he memorialized asking to return to Chang'an. Soon afterward Zhang Congbin's rebellion erupted in Luoyang; Yun alone escaped harm, and all agreed that he truly enjoyed the full measure of the five blessings.
value.literal: In the second year of Tianfu he memorialized asking to return to Chang'an. Soon Zhang Congbin's rebellion broke out in Luoyang; Yun alone escaped the calamity, and everyone said Yun truly possessed the full beauty of the five blessings.

value.zh: 是歲，卒於家。
value.en: That year he died at home.
value.literal: That year he died at home.

value.zh: 贈太子太師。
value.en: He was posthumously awarded the title Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
value.literal: Posthumously awarded Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

value.zh: 弟篯。
value.en: Younger brother Jian.
value.literal: Younger brother Jian.

value.zh: 篯，字慕彭，少嗜酒無節，為鄉里所鄙。
value.en: Jian, courtesy name Mupeng, was in his youth addicted to wine without restraint and was despised in his home district.
value.literal: Jian, style name Mupeng, in youth was addicted to wine without restraint and was despised by his district.

value.zh: 唐天復中，兄筠為大梁四鎮客將，篯自海州省兄，兄薦於兗州連帥王瓚，用為裨校。
value.en: During the Tianfu era of the Tang dynasty (901–904), his elder brother Yun served as guest general of Daliang's four commands. Jian traveled from Haizhou to visit him; Yun recommended him to the Yanzhou commander Wang Zan, who took him on as adjutant.
value.literal: In the Tianfu era of the Tang dynasty (901–904), his elder brother Yun was guest general of the four commands of Daliang; Jian came from Haizhou to visit his brother, and Yun recommended him to the Yanzhou commander Wang Zan, who employed him as adjutant.

value.zh: 篯性桀黠，善事人，累遷軍職。
value.en: Jian was clever and crafty by nature, adept at winning people over, and rose repeatedly through military ranks.
value.literal: Jian's nature was clever and crafty; he was skilled at pleasing people and was repeatedly promoted in military posts.

value.zh: 後唐莊宗都洛，筠鎮長安，自衙內指揮使授檢校司空、右千牛衛將軍同正，領饒州刺史、西京管內三白渠營田制置使。
value.en: When Emperor Zhuangzong of Later Tang established his capital at Luoyang, Yun garrisoned Chang'an. From palace-inner commander he was made acting Minister of Works and Right Imperial Equerry General with concurrent appointment, and concurrently served as prefect of Raozhou and commissioner for the three Baibi canals farming administration in the western capital circuit.
value.literal: When Later Tang Emperor Zhuangzong made Luoyang his capital, Yun garrisoned Chang'an; from palace-inner commander he was appointed acting Minister of Works, Right Imperial Equerry General with concurrent appointment, and concurrently Raozhou prefect and commissioner for the three Baibi canals farming administration within the western capital circuit.

value.zh: 同光末，筠隨魏王繼岌伐蜀，奏篯權知西京留守事。
value.en: At the end of the Tongguang era Yun followed the Prince of Wei, Li Jiji, on the campaign against Shu and memorialized to have Jian provisionally handle western capital garrison affairs.
value.literal: At the end of Tongguang, Yun followed the Prince of Wei Li Jiji in the expedition against Shu and memorialized to have Jian provisionally administer western capital garrison affairs.

value.zh: 蜀平，王衍挈族入朝，至秦川驛，莊宗遣中使向延嗣乘驛騎盡戮王衍之族，所有奇貨，盡歸於延嗣。
value.en: After Shu was pacified, Wang Yan led his clan to court. At Qinchuan post station Zhuangzong sent the palace envoy Xiang Yansi on relay horses to slaughter Wang Yan's entire clan; all rare goods went entirely to Yansi.
value.literal: When Shu was pacified, Wang Yan led his clan to court. At Qinchuan post station Zhuangzong sent palace envoy Xiang Yansi on post-horses to slaughter Wang Yan's entire clan; all rare goods fell entirely to Yansi.

value.zh: 俄聞莊宗遇內難，繼岌軍次興平，篯乃斷咸陽浮橋，繼岌浮渡至渭南死之，一行金寶妓樂，篯悉獲之。
value.en: Soon word arrived that Zhuangzong had met with internal disaster. Li Jiji's army halted at Xingping; Jian cut the Xianyang floating bridge, and Jiji crossed by raft to Weinan, where he died. Jian seized the whole train of gold, jewels, and entertainers.
value.literal: Soon word came that Zhuangzong had met internal disaster. Li Jiji's army halted at Xingping; Jian severed the Xianyang floating bridge, Jiji crossed by raft to Weinan and died there; the entire train of gold, jewels, and entertainers Jian seized entirely.
